author.name: Haesung Oh, Jaesung Lee

entry.summary: Proposes wavelet-based cross-band integration for polyp segmentation, showing that grayscale wavelet representations preserve higher boundary contrast than RGB, improving boundary delineation for colorectal cancer detection.

entry.title: An Adaptive KKT-Based Indicator for Convergence Assessment in Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Thiago Santos, Sebastiao Xavier

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive KKT-based convergence indicator for multi-objective optimization that uses quantile-based reformulation to assess convergence without relying on known Pareto fronts.

entry.title: OmniPlanner: Universal Exploration and Inspection Path Planning across Robot Morphologies

author.name: Angelos Zacharia, Mihir Dharmadhikari, Mohit Singh, Kostas Alexis

entry.summary: Presents OmniPlanner, a unified path planning framework that works across aerial, ground, and underwater robots for exploration and inspection tasks, using a platform abstraction layer to handle morphology-specific constraints.

entry.title: Statistical Inference for Score Decompositions

author.name: Timo Dimitriadis, Marius Puke

entry.summary: Introduces inference methods for score decompositions that partition predictive scoring functions into miscalibration, discrimination, and uncertainty components, connecting to Mincer-Zarnowitz regression and enabling formal tests for equal forecast quality.

entry.title: The Influence of Iconicity in Transfer Learning for Sign Language Recognition

author.name: Keren Artiaga, Conor Lynch, Haithem Afli, Mohammed Hasanuzzaman

entry.summary: Examines transfer learning for sign language recognition by comparing iconic sign similarity effects across different sign language pairs, using MediaPipe features with MLP and GRU architectures.

entry.title: Learning Order Forest for Qualitative-Attribute Data Clustering

author.name: Mingjie Zhao, Sen Feng, Yiqun Zhang, Mengke Li, Yang Lu, Yiu-ming Cheung

entry.summary: Proposes a tree-like distance structure for clustering qualitative attribute data, capturing order relationships among nominal values via a joint learning mechanism.

entry.title: Baseline Performance of AI Tools in Classifying Cognitive Demand of Mathematical Tasks

author.name: Danielle S. Fox, Brenda L. Robles, Elizabeth DiPietro Brovey, Christian D. Schunn

entry.summary: Evaluates 11 AI tools (general-purpose and education-specific) on classifying the cognitive demand level of mathematical tasks. Tests how well current LLMs can support teachers in curriculum adaptation.

entry.title: mlx-snn: Spiking Neural Networks on Apple Silicon via MLX

author.name: Jiahao Qin

entry.summary: Introduces mlx-snn, the first spiking neural network library built natively on Apple's MLX framework, providing neuron models, surrogate gradients, spike encoding, and BPTT training for Apple Silicon.

entry.title: Towards Effective Orchestration of AI x DB Workloads

author.name: Naili Xing, Haotian Gao, Zhanhao Zhao, Shaofeng Cai, Zhaojing Luo, Yuncheng Wu, Zhongle Xie, Meihui Zhang, Beng Chin Ooi

entry.summary: Discusses challenges of integrating AI workloads directly into database engines, addressing joint query processing, model execution optimization, resource coordination, and security in multi-tenant systems.

entry.title: Towards Generalized Multimodal Homography Estimation

author.name: Jinkun You, Jiaxin Cheng, Jie Zhang, Yicong Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes a training data synthesis method for generalized multimodal homography estimation that generates unaligned image pairs from single images. Achieves cross-modality generalization without needing modality-specific training data.

entry.title: A Multi-Dimensional Quality Scoring Framework for Decentralized LLM Inference with Proof of Quality

author.name: Arther Tian, Alex Ding, Frank Chen, Simon Wu, Aaron Chan

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-dimensional quality scoring framework for decentralized LLM inference networks, decomposing output quality into modular dimensions including structure, semantics, alignment, and agreement. Extends Proof of Quality mechanisms for incentive-compatible quality assessment.

entry.title: Efficient Point Cloud Processing with High-Dimensional Positional Encoding and Non-Local MLPs

author.name: Yanmei Zou, Hongshan Yu, Yaonan Wang, Zhengeng Yang, Xieyuanli Chen, Kailun Yang, Naveed Akhtar

entry.summary: Proposes efficient point cloud processing using high-dimensional positional encoding and non-local MLPs. Develops a two-stage abstraction-refinement view for modular feature extraction that clarifies the evolution of point cloud architectures.

entry.title: When Small Variations Become Big Failures: Reliability Challenges in Compute-in-Memory Neural Accelerators

author.name: Yifan Qin, Jiahao Zheng, Zheyu Yan, Wujie Wen, Xiaobo Sharon Hu, Yiyu Shi

entry.summary: Examines reliability challenges in compute-in-memory neural accelerators, showing small device variations can cause disproportionate failures. Presents techniques bridging device physics, architecture, and learning algorithms.

entry.title: Logit-Level Uncertainty Quantification in Vision-Language Models for Histopathology Image Analysis

author.name: Betul Yurdem, Ferhat Ozgur Catak, Murat Kuzlu, Mehmet Kemal Gullu

entry.summary: Proposes a logit-level uncertainty quantification framework for VLMs in histopathology, using temperature-controlled output logits to separate model confidence from uncertainty.

entry.title: Freezing of Gait Prediction using Proactive Agent that Learns from Selected Experience and DDQN Algorithm

author.name: Septian Enggar Sukmana (Kyushu Institute of Technology), Sang Won Bae (Stevens Institute of Technology), Tomohiro Shibata (Kyushu Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Applies Double Deep Q-Network with Prioritized Experience Replay to predict Freezing of Gait episodes in Parkinson's Disease patients. Aims to extend the prediction horizon for proactive assistive interventions.

entry.title: Multi-Stage Music Source Restoration with BandSplit-RoFormer Separation and HiFi++ GAN

author.name: Tobias Morocutti, Emmanouil Karystinaios, Jonathan Greif, Gerhard Widmer

entry.summary: Presents a multi-stage music source restoration system using BandSplit-RoFormer separation with curriculum training and instrument-specific HiFi++ GAN restorers for the MSR ICASSP Challenge.

entry.title: Enhancing Authorship Attribution with Synthetic Paintings

author.name: Clarissa Loures, Caio Hosken, Luan Oliveira, Gianlucca Zuin, Adriano Veloso

entry.summary: Investigates whether synthetic images generated via DreamBooth fine-tuning of Stable Diffusion can improve painting authorship attribution models. A hybrid real+synthetic approach achieves higher accuracy than real-only training.

entry.title: Adaptive Enhancement and Dual-Pooling Sequential Attention for Lightweight Underwater Object Detection with YOLOv10

author.name: Md. Mushibur Rahman, Umme Fawzia Rahim, Enam Ahmed Taufik

entry.summary: Introduces a lightweight underwater object detection framework based on YOLOv10 with adaptive enhancement, dual-pooling attention, and focal generalized IoU objectness for handling challenging underwater conditions.

entry.title: Long-Term Visual Localization in Dynamic Benthic Environments: A Dataset, Footprint-Based Ground Truth, and Visual Place Recognition Benchmark

author.name: Martin Kvisvik Larsen, Oscar Pizarro

entry.summary: Presents a curated dataset and novel ground-truthing method for long-term visual localization in underwater benthic environments using AUV imagery, addressing the lack of benchmarks for this domain.

entry.title: CLIP-Guided Multi-Task Regression for Multi-View Plant Phenotyping

author.name: Simon Warmers, Muhammad Zawish, Fayaz Ali Dharejo, Steven Davy, Radu Timofte

entry.summary: Proposes a CLIP-based multi-task framework for multi-view plant phenotyping that jointly predicts plant age and leaf count, achieving substantial improvements over baselines on the GroMo25 benchmark.

entry.title: LISTA-Transformer Model Based on Sparse Coding and Attention Mechanism and Its Application in Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Shuang Liu, Lina Zhao, Tian Wang, Huaqing Wang

entry.summary: Proposes LISTA-Transformer combining sparse coding (LISTA) with attention mechanisms for joint local feature modeling and global dependency capture, applied to image classification and industrial fault diagnosis.

entry.title: HBRB-BoW: A Retrained Bag-of-Words Vocabulary for ORB-SLAM via Hierarchical BRB-KMeans

author.name: Minjae Lee, Sang-Min Choi, Gun-Woo Kim, Suwon Lee

entry.summary: Proposes HBRB-BoW, a refined hierarchical binary vocabulary for ORB-SLAM that addresses precision loss in conventional binary clustering by converting to real-valued space for clustering and back to binary.

entry.title: Passive Phase-Oriented Impedance Shaping for Rapid Acceleration in Soft Robotic Swimmers

author.name: Qimin Feng, Orion A. Roberts, Qiang Zhong

entry.summary: Investigates constrained-layer damping as a passive mechanism for frequency-selective impedance shaping in soft robotic swimmers, showing how it enhances thrust and phase relationships for rapid acceleration.

entry.title: Swimming Under Constraints: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Framework for Quadrupedal Bio-Inspired Propulsion

entry.title: Research Summary: March 04, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by foundational advances in alignment theory and a strong cluster of AI safety work spanning agentic systems, cybersecurity, and content authentication.

  • The Latent Value Hypothesis offers the first theoretical explanation for why RLAIF succeeds, grounding it in geometric structure of pretrained representations
  • A systematic Meta study (LeCun, Xie, Zettlemoyer) clarifies native multimodal pretraining design tradeoffs across vision-language architectures
  • Scaling reward modeling without human supervision via web-corpus preference learning could dramatically reduce alignment data costs
  • A first formal theoretical separation shows why Adam achieves sharper tail convergence than SGD, resolving a long-standing empirical puzzle

Safety and security research is notably strong: ZeroDayBench tests frontier models on real zero-day vulnerability discovery; MOSAIC introduces plan-check-act-or-refuse for safe agentic tool use; and safety training is shown to persist through helpfulness optimization in agentic settings. The Integrity Clash paper exposes a fundamental conflict between C2PA provenance and AI watermarking, undermining deployed authentication infrastructure. On the efficiency side, Speculative Speculative Decoding parallelizes speculation and verification for practical inference speedups.

entry.title: Why Does RLAIF Work At All?

author.name: Robin Young

entry.summary: Proposes the 'latent value hypothesis' to explain why RLAIF works: pretraining encodes human values as directions in representation space, and constitutional prompts act as projection operators to elicit these latent values. Formalizes this under a linear model and derives conditions for when RLAIF succeeds or fails.

entry.title: Beyond Language Modeling: An Exploration of Multimodal Pretraining

author.name: Shengbang Tong, David Fan, John Nguyen, Ellis Brown, Gaoyue Zhou, Shengyi Qian, Boyang Zheng, Th\'eophane Vallaeys, Junlin Han, Rob Fergus, Naila Murray, Marjan Ghazvininejad, Mike Lewis, Nicolas Ballas, Amir Bar, Michael Rabbat, Jakob Verbeek, Luke Zettlemoyer, Koustuv Sinha, Yann LeCun, Saining Xie

entry.summary: This paper from a strong team (including Yann LeCun, Saining Xie, and Meta researchers) provides empirical clarity on native multimodal pretraining design space through controlled from-scratch experiments using the Transfusion framework with next-token prediction for language and diffusion for vision, yielding insights about visual representation, data mixing, and emergent cross-modal capabilities.

entry.title: Scaling Reward Modeling without Human Supervision

author.name: Jingxuan Fan, Yueying Li, Zhenting Qi, Dinghuai Zhang, Kiant\'e Brantley, Sham M. Kakade, Hanlin Zhang

entry.summary: Explores scaling reward models through unsupervised approaches using preference learning over document prefixes/suffixes from web corpora, without human annotations. Shows that training on 11M tokens of math-focused web data yields consistent gains on RewardBench across multiple backbone models.

entry.title: ZeroDayBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Unseen Zero-Day Vulnerabilities for Cyberdefense

entry.summary: Introduces ZeroDayBench, a benchmark where LLM agents must find and patch 22 novel critical vulnerabilities in open-source codebases. Tests GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Grok 4.1, finding frontier LLMs are not yet capable of autonomously solving these tasks.

entry.title: Why Adam Can Beat SGD: Second-Moment Normalization Yields Sharper Tails

author.name: Ruinan Jin, Yingbin Liang, Shaofeng Zou

entry.summary: Establishes the first theoretical separation between high-probability convergence of Adam and SGD, showing Adam achieves δ^{-1/2} dependence on confidence parameter while SGD necessarily has δ^{-1} dependence. Attributes this to Adam's second-moment normalization creating sharper tail behavior.

author.name: Aradhye Agarwal, Gurdit Siyan, Yash Pandya, Joykirat Singh, Akshay Nambi, Ahmed Awadallah

entry.summary: Introduces MOSAIC, a post-training framework for safe multi-step agentic tool use that structures inference as 'plan, check, then act or refuse' with explicit safety reasoning and refusal as first-class learning objectives.

entry.title: Quantifying Frontier LLM Capabilities for Container Sandbox Escape

entry.title: The Geometry of Learning Under AI Delegation

author.name: Lingxiao Huang, Nisheeth K. Vishnoi

entry.summary: Mathematically models the joint evolution of human skill and AI delegation as a coupled dynamical system, revealing that adaptive AI use creates stable low-skill equilibria where humans can become persistently dependent on AI ('learned helplessness'). Shows that beyond the high-skill equilibrium of human-only learning, AI delegation fundamentally alters skill acquisition dynamics.

entry.title: Safety Training Persists Through Helpfulness Optimization in LLM Agents

author.name: Benjamin Plaut

entry.summary: Studies safety training persistence in agentic (multi-step, tool-use) LLM settings, finding that safety training persists through subsequent helpfulness DPO training, unlike findings in single-step chat settings. All training configurations converge near a linear Pareto frontier.

entry.title: BeyondSWE: Can Current Code Agent Survive Beyond Single-Repo Bug Fixing?

entry.title: Subspace Geometry Governs Catastrophic Forgetting in Low-Rank Adaptation

entry.title: ACE-Brain-0: Spatial Intelligence as a Shared Scaffold for Universal Embodiments

author.name: Ziyang Gong, Zehang Luo, Anke Tang, Zhe Liu, Shi Fu, Zhi Hou, Ganlin Yang, Weiyun Wang, Xiaofeng Wang, Jianbo Liu, Gen Luo, Haolan Kang, Shuang Luo, Yue Zhou, Yong Luo, Li Shen, Xiaosong Jia, Yao Mu, Xue Yang, Chunxiao Liu, Junchi Yan, Hengshuang Zhao, Dacheng Tao, Xiaogang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces ACE-Brain-0, a generalist foundation model unifying spatial reasoning, autonomous driving, and robotic manipulation within a single multimodal LLM, using spatial intelligence as a shared scaffold across diverse embodiments.

entry.title: Authenticated Contradictions from Desynchronized Provenance and Watermarking

entry.title: PRISM: Pushing the Frontier of Deep Think via Process Reward Model-Guided Inference

author.name: Junfeng Fang, Nachuan Chen, Houcheng Jiang, Dan Zhang, Fei Shen, Xiang Wang, Xiangnan He, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Introduces NExT-Guard, a training-free streaming safeguard that monitors interpretable latent features from Sparse Autoencoders to interdict unsafe content in real-time, challenging the assumption that streaming safety requires token-level supervised training.

entry.title: SAE as a Crystal Ball: Interpretable Features Predict Cross-domain Transferability of LLMs without Training

author.name: Qi Zhang, Yifei Wang, Xiaohan Wang, Jiajun Chai, Guojun Yin, Wei Lin, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: Proposes SAE-based Transferability Score (STS) using sparse autoencoders to predict how post-training (e.g., fine-tuning) will transfer across domains without actually training, identifying shifted dimensions in SAE feature space as predictive of transfer performance.

entry.title: SUN: Shared Use of Next-token Prediction for Efficient Multi-LLM Disaggregated Serving

author.name: Sunghyeon Woo, Ahreum Seo, Jaegwang Lee, Jaeeun Kil, Hanbae Seo, Joonghoon Kim, Baeseong Park, Se Jung Kwon, Dongsoo Lee

entry.summary: Proposes SUN (Shared Use of Next-token Prediction), enabling cross-model sharing of decode execution in disaggregated multi-LLM serving by decomposing transformers into prefill and decode modules, where only the prefill module is fine-tuned per task.

entry.title: Param$\Delta$ for Direct Weight Mixing: Post-Train Large Language Model at Zero Cost

author.name: Sheng Cao, Mingrui Wu, Karthik Prasad, Yuandong Tian, Zechun Liu

entry.summary: Introduces ParamΔ, a method that transfers post-training knowledge to newly updated base models with zero additional training by computing weight differences between post-trained and base models and applying them to new base models.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Preferences: A Principled Framework for Reward Modeling with Ordinal Feedback

author.name: Amirhossein Afsharrad, Ruida Zhou, Luca Viano, Sanjay Lall, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh

entry.summary: Presents a theoretically grounded framework for reward modeling with ordinal (Likert scale) preferences, formulating it as discrete ordinal regression rather than using ad-hoc heuristics on top of binary preference models like Bradley-Terry.

entry.title: Silent Sabotage During Fine-Tuning: Few-Shot Rationale Poisoning of Compact Medical LLMs

author.name: Jingyuan Xie, Wenjie Wang, Ji Wu, Jiandong Gao

entry.summary: Proposes a novel poisoning attack targeting the reasoning process of medical LLMs during supervised fine-tuning by injecting poisoned rationales rather than traditional backdoor triggers. Demonstrates stealthy degradation of model performance on targeted medical topics.

entry.title: Contextualized Privacy Defense for LLM Agents

author.name: Yule Wen, Yanzhe Zhang, Jianxun Lian, Xiaoyuan Yi, Xing Xie, Diyi Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Contextualized Defense Instructing (CDI), a privacy defense paradigm for LLM agents where an instructor model generates step-specific, context-aware privacy guidance during multi-step agent execution. Uses reinforcement learning to optimize the instructor model based on execution outcomes.

entry.title: UniG2U-Bench: Do Unified Models Advance Multimodal Understanding?

author.name: Zimo Wen, Boxiu Li, Wanbo Zhang, Junxiang Lei, Xiaoyu Chen, Yijia Fan, Qi Zhang, Yujiang Wang, Lili Qiu, Bo Li, Ziwei Liu, Caihua Shan, Yifan Yang, Yifei Shen

entry.summary: Introduces UniG2U-Bench, a benchmark evaluating whether generation capabilities improve understanding in unified multimodal models, across 7 regimes and 30 subtasks. Finds that unified models generally underperform their base VLMs, and Generate-then-Answer inference typically degrades performance.

entry.title: From Shallow to Deep: Pinning Semantic Intent via Causal GRPO

author.name: Shuyi Zhou, Zeen Song, Wenwen Qiang, Jiyan Sun, Yao Zhou, Yinlong Liu, Wei Ma

entry.summary: Diagnoses LLM vulnerability to adversarial prefix attacks as 'Shallow Safety Alignment' caused by semantic representation decay, and proposes TSC-GRPO using causal intent probes and group relative policy optimization to achieve 'intent pinning'.

entry.title: CUCo: An Agentic Framework for Compute and Communication Co-design

author.name: Bodun Hu, Yoga Sri Varshan V, Saurabh Agarwal, Aditya Akella

entry.summary: CUCo is an agent-driven framework that automatically generates high-performance CUDA kernels jointly optimizing computation and communication for distributed LLM training/inference, without requiring training.

entry.title: CFG-Ctrl: Control-Based Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance

author.name: Hanyang Wang, Yiyang Liu, Jiawei Chi, Fangfu Liu, Ran Xue, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: Proposes CFG-Ctrl, a framework that reinterprets Classifier-Free Guidance in diffusion models as a control problem, moving beyond linear (P-control) approaches to nonlinear control laws. This addresses instability, overshooting, and degraded fidelity at large guidance scales in flow-based diffusion models.

entry.title: ACE-Merging: Data-Free Model Merging with Adaptive Covariance Estimation

author.name: Bo Xu, Haotian Wu, Hehai Lin, Weiquan Huang, Beier Zhu, Yao Shu, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: Introduces ACE-Merging, a data-free model merging method that estimates input covariance from parameter differences of fine-tuned models, enabling optimal merging of task-specific experts without data access, retraining, or architectural changes.

entry.title: Evaluating Performance Drift from Model Switching in Multi-Turn LLM Systems

author.name: Raad Khraishi, Iman Zafar, Katie Myles, Greig A Cowan

entry.summary: Introduces a switch-matrix benchmark measuring performance drift when different LLM models are swapped mid-conversation in multi-turn systems. Finds single-turn handoffs can cause -8 to +13 point swings, revealing a previously understudied deployment risk.

entry.title: MERG3R: A Divide-and-Conquer Approach to Large-Scale Neural Visual Geometry

author.name: Leo Kaixuan Cheng, Abdus Shaikh, Ruofan Liang, Zhijie Wu, Yushi Guan, Nandita Vijaykumar

entry.summary: Introduces MERG3R, a training-free divide-and-conquer framework enabling neural visual geometry models (like VGGT) to scale beyond GPU memory limits for large-scale 3D reconstruction by partitioning, reconstructing, and merging image subsets.

entry.title: Designing UNICORN: a Unified Benchmark for Imaging in Computational Pathology, Radiology, and Natural Language

author.name: Michelle Stegeman (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Lena Philipp (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Fennie van der Graaf (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Marina D'Amato (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Cl\'ement Grisi (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Luc Builtjes (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Joeran S. Bosma (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Judith Lefkes (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Rianne A. Weber (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), James A. Meakin (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Thomas Koopman (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Anne Mickan (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Mathias Prokop (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Ewoud J. Smit (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Geert Litjens (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Jeroen van der Laak (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Bram van Ginneken (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Maarten de Rooij (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Henkjan Huisman (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Colin Jacobs (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Francesco Ciompi (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium), Alessa Hering (and on behalf of the UNICORN consortium)

entry.summary: UNICORN is a unified public benchmark for systematically evaluating medical foundation models across pathology, radiology, and natural language under a standardized protocol. It uses a novel two-step framework to isolate representation quality, addressing the fragmentation of existing medical AI benchmarks across modality- and task-specific settings.

entry.title: A Tale of Three Contracts

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's detailed analysis of three contracts between Anthropic, OpenAI, and the Department of War, providing context for the DoW's attempt to label Anthropic as a supply chain risk. Covers what is publicly known about the contract negotiations and their implications.

entry.title: SorryDB: Can AI Provers Complete Real-World Lean Theorems?

author.name: Austin Letson, Leopoldo Sarra, Auguste Poiroux, Oliver Dressler, Paul Lezeau, Dhyan Aranha, Frederick Pu, Aaron Hill, Miguel Corredera Hidalgo, Julian Berman, George Tsoukalas, Lenny Taelman

entry.summary: Introduces SorryDB, a dynamically-updating benchmark of open Lean proof tasks drawn from 78 real-world formalization projects on GitHub, designed to evaluate AI theorem provers on practical mathematics while mitigating contamination through continuous updates.

entry.title: Self-Play Only Evolves When Self-Synthetic Pipeline Ensures Learnable Information Gain

author.name: Wei Liu, Siya Qi, Yali Du, Yulan He

entry.summary: Demonstrates that sustainable self-play evolution in LLMs requires self-synthesized data with increasing learnable information across iterations, identifying three key roles (Proposer, Solver, Verifier) and three system designs that enable this.

entry.title: Neural Paging: Learning Context Management Policies for Turing-Complete Agents

author.name: Liang Chen, Qi Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Paging, a hierarchical architecture that manages LLM context windows as semantic caches, formulating the Context Paging Problem and proposing a differentiable Page Controller to approximate 'Semantic Belady's Optimality'.

entry.title: CoDAR: Continuous Diffusion Language Models are More Powerful Than You Think

author.name: Junzhe Shen, Jieru Zhao, Ziwei He, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: Identifies token rounding as the primary bottleneck for continuous diffusion language models and proposes CoDAR, using an autoregressive transformer decoder for context-conditional discretization, achieving SOTA for continuous DLMs on LM1B and OpenWebText.

entry.title: Length Generalization Bounds for Transformers

author.name: Andy Yang, Pascal Bergstr\"a{\ss}er, Georg Zetzsche, David Chiang, Anthony W. Lin

entry.summary: Proves that length generalization bounds for CRASP (a transformer-linked language class) are generally non-computable, establishing fundamental limits. Provides both positive results for restricted cases and negative results for the general case.

entry.title: PrivMedChat: End-to-End Differentially Private RLHF for Medical Dialogue Systems

author.name: Sudip Bhujel

entry.summary: Presents PrivMedChat, an end-to-end differentially private RLHF framework for medical dialogue systems that enforces DP at every training stage accessing dialogue-derived supervision, addressing memorization risks in clinical LLM applications.

entry.title: StitchCUDA: An Automated Multi-Agents End-to-End GPU Programing Framework with Rubric-based Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shiyang Li, Zijian Zhang, Winson Chen, Yuebo Luo, Mingyi Hong, Caiwen Ding

entry.summary: Proposes StitchCUDA, a multi-agent framework for end-to-end GPU program generation with specialized Planner, Coder, and Verifier agents, using rubric-based agentic reinforcement learning to optimize CUDA performance beyond single-kernel optimization.

entry.title: BRIGHT: A Collaborative Generalist-Specialist Foundation Model for Breast Pathology

author.name: Xiaojing Guo, Jiatai Lin, Yumian Jia, Jingqi Huang, Zeyan Xu, Weidong Li, Longfei Wang, Jingjing Chen, Qin Li, Weiwei Wang, Lifang Cui, Wen Yue, Zhiqiang Cheng, Xiaolong Wei, Jianzhong Yu, Xia Jin, Baizhou Li, Honghong Shen, Jing Li, Chunlan Li, Yanfen Cui, Yi Dai, Yiling Yang, Xiaolong Qian, Liu Yang, Yang Yang, Guangshen Gao, Yaqing Li, Lili Zhai, Chenying Liu, Tianhua Zhang, Zhenwei Shi, Cheng Lu, Xingchen Zhou, Jing Xu, Miaoqing Zhao, Fang Mei, Jiaojiao Zhou, Ning Mao, Fangfang Liu, Chu Han, Zaiyi Liu

entry.summary: BRIGHT is the first pathology foundation model specifically designed for breast pathology, trained on ~210 million histopathology tiles from over 5,000 cases using a collaborative generalist-specialist training paradigm to translate broad histomorphological knowledge into organ-specific expertise.

entry.title: Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks in LLM Agent Memory

author.name: Boqin Yuan, Yue Su, Kun Yao

entry.summary: Introduces a diagnostic framework analyzing retrieval vs. utilization bottlenecks in LLM agent memory, finding retrieval method is the dominant factor (20-point accuracy span) while write strategy matters much less (3-8 points). Raw chunked storage surprisingly performs competitively.

entry.title: Architecting Trust in Artificial Epistemic Agents

author.name: Nahema Marchal, Stephanie Chan, Matija Franklin, Manon Revel, Geoff Keeling, Roberta Fischli, Bilva Chandra, Iason Gabriel

entry.summary: Argues that LLMs increasingly function as epistemic agents that shape knowledge environments, and proposes a framework for architecting trust in these systems considering their impact on knowledge creation, curation, and synthesis. Authors include Anthropic/DeepMind researchers.

entry.title: Density-Guided Response Optimization: Community-Grounded Alignment via Implicit Acceptance Signals

author.name: Patrick Gerard, Svitlana Volkova

entry.summary: Proposes Density-Guided Response Optimization, a method for aligning language models to community norms using implicit acceptance signals (what content persists in communities) rather than explicit preference labels, leveraging geometric structure in representation space.

entry.title: Is Retraining-Free Enough? The Necessity of Router Calibration for Efficient MoE Compression

author.name: Sieun Hyeon, Jaeyoung Do

entry.summary: Shows that router-expert mismatch is a key source of degradation in retraining-free MoE compression, and proposes Router Knowledge Distillation that updates only the router (tiny fraction of parameters) to restore performance.

entry.title: Social-JEPA: Emergent Geometric Isomorphism

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Youjin Wang, Yi Duan, Rong Fu, Dianyu Zhao, Sicheng Fan, Shuaishuai Cao, Wentao Guo, Xiao Zhou

entry.summary: Shows that separate agents learning world models from distinct viewpoints of the same environment develop latent spaces related by approximate linear isometry, enabling zero-shot transfer of classifiers between agents without additional training.

entry.title: Preconditioned Score and Flow Matching

author.name: Shadab Ahamed, Eshed Gal, Simon Ghyselincks, Md Shahriar Rahim Siddiqui, Moshe Eliasof, Eldad Haber

entry.summary: Proposes preconditioned score/flow matching that reshapes the geometry of intermediate distributions to fix optimization bias caused by ill-conditioned covariance, improving learning of low-variance modes without altering the generative model.

entry.title: Conditioned Activation Transport for T2I Safety Steering

author.name: Maciej Chrab\k{a}szcz, Aleksander Szymczyk, Jan Dubi\'nski, Tomasz Trzci\'nski, Franziska Boenisch, Adam Dziedzic

entry.summary: Proposes Conditioned Activation Transport (CAT) for T2I safety steering that uses geometry-based conditioning and nonlinear transport maps to suppress unsafe image generation while minimizing quality degradation on benign prompts. Introduces SafeSteerDataset with 2300 contrastive safe/unsafe prompt pairs.

entry.title: Understanding and Mitigating Dataset Corruption in LLM Steering

author.name: Cullen Anderson, Narmeen Oozeer, Foad Namjoo, Remy Ogasawara, Amirali Abdullah, Jeff M. Phillips

entry.summary: Studies robustness of contrastive steering for LLMs under dataset corruption, finding it surprisingly robust to moderate corruption but showing that adversarial corruption can degrade performance. Proposes ROCS, a robust contrastive steering method resilient to corruption.

entry.title: Dimension-Independent Convergence of Underdamped Langevin Monte Carlo in KL Divergence

author.name: Shiyuan Zhang, Qiwei Di, Xuheng Li, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: Proves the first dimension-free KL divergence bounds for discretized underdamped Langevin dynamics, closing a gap between Wasserstein and KL convergence guarantees for this widely-used sampler.

entry.title: The Price of Robustness: Stable Classifiers Need Overparameterization

author.name: Jonas von Berg, Adalbert Fono, Massimiliano Datres, Sohir Maskey, Gitta Kutyniok

entry.summary: Establishes generalization bounds for classifiers that improve with class stability (margin), deriving a law of robustness for classification showing that interpolating models with p≈n parameters must be unstable, requiring substantial overparameterization for robustness.

entry.title: CGL: Advancing Continual GUI Learning via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning

author.name: Zhenquan Yao, Zitong Huang, Yihan Zeng, Jianhua Han, Hang Xu, Chun-Mei Feng, Jianwei Ma, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: Reveals that reinforcement learning is more resilient to catastrophic forgetting than supervised fine-tuning for GUI agents, and proposes CGL framework that dynamically balances RL and SFT for continual learning of GUI tasks.

entry.title: Sparse autoencoders reveal organized biological knowledge but minimal regulatory logic in single-cell foundation models: a comparative atlas of Geneformer and scGPT

author.name: Ihor Kendiukhov

entry.summary: Applies sparse autoencoders to single-cell foundation models (Geneformer, scGPT), finding organized biological knowledge but minimal regulatory logic, with 99.8% of features invisible to SVD confirming massive superposition.

entry.title: ExpGuard: LLM Content Moderation in Specialized Domains

author.name: Minseok Choi, Dongjin Kim, Seungbin Yang, Subin Kim, Youngjun Kwak, Juyoung Oh, Jaegul Choo, Jungmin Son

entry.summary: Introduces ExpGuard, a specialized guardrail model for content moderation in financial, medical, and legal domains, along with ExpGuardMix dataset (58,928 labeled samples). Addresses the gap where general-purpose guardrails fail on domain-specific jargon and adversarial content.

entry.title: Nodes Are Early, Edges Are Late: Probing Diagram Representations in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Haruto Yoshida, Keito Kudo, Yoichi Aoki, Ryota Tanaka, Itsumi Saito, Keisuke Sakaguchi, Kentaro Inui

entry.summary: Probes how large vision-language models internally represent diagrams, finding that node information is encoded early in vision encoders while edge/relationship information only emerges later in language model text tokens. Reveals a key bottleneck for diagram understanding.

entry.title: Track4World: Feedforward World-centric Dense 3D Tracking of All Pixels

author.name: Jiahao Lu, Jiayi Xu, Wenbo Hu, Ruijie Zhu, Chengfeng Zhao, Sai-Kit Yeung, Ying Shan, Yuan Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Track4World, a feedforward model for dense 3D tracking of every pixel in world-centric coordinates from monocular video, using VGGT-style ViT with a novel 3D correlation scheme for simultaneous 2D and 3D flow estimation.

entry.title: Neural Electromagnetic Fields for High-Resolution Material Parameter Reconstruction

author.name: Zhe Chen, Peilin Zheng, Wenshuo Chen, Xiucheng Wang, Yutao Yue, Nan Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces NEMF (Neural Electromagnetic Fields) for dense, non-invasive reconstruction of material properties (permittivity, conductivity) to create functional digital twins, solving the ill-posed physical inversion problem using combined visual and RF signals.

entry.title: Think-as-You-See: Streaming Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jialiang Zhang, Junlong Tong, Junyan Lin, Hao Wu, Yirong Sun, Yunpu Ma, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Think-as-You-See (TaYS) introduces a streaming chain-of-thought reasoning framework for Large Vision-Language Models that enables concurrent reasoning as video frames arrive, rather than requiring full-video availability. This better aligns with real-world video stream processing.

entry.title: Utonia: Toward One Encoder for All Point Clouds

author.name: Yujia Zhang, Xiaoyang Wu, Yunhan Yang, Xianzhe Fan, Han Li, Yuechen Zhang, Zehao Huang, Naiyan Wang, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: Utonia trains a single self-supervised point transformer encoder across diverse domains (remote sensing, LiDAR, indoor RGB-D, CAD, RGB-lifted point clouds), learning a consistent representation space that transfers across domains with emergent cross-domain behaviors.

entry.title: ULTRA: Unified Multimodal Control for Autonomous Humanoid Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Xialin He, Sirui Xu, Xinyao Li, Runpei Dong, Liuyu Bian, Yu-Xiong Wang, Liang-Yan Gui

entry.summary: ULTRA proposes a unified framework for autonomous humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation with physics-driven neural retargeting from MoCap data and perception-driven behavior generation, moving beyond tracking predefined motion references.

entry.title: White-Box Attacks on the Best Open-Weight Model: CCP Bias vs. Safety Training in Kimi K2.5

author.name: Corm

entry.summary: Demonstrates white-box attacks on Kimi K2.5 (described as the best open-weight model) using steering vectors and input manipulation to bypass safety training and remove CCP bias. Successfully got the model to answer HarmBench questions in detail using cheap interventions like mean difference, SVD, PCA, and linear probes.

entry.title: Guideline-Grounded Evidence Accumulation for High-Stakes Agent Verification

author.name: Yichi Zhang, Nabeel Seedat, Yinpeng Dong, Peng Cui, Jun Zhu, Mihaela van de Schaar

entry.summary: Establishes GLEAN, an agent verification framework using guideline-grounded evidence accumulation that compiles expert protocols into trajectory-informed correctness signals, calibrated along agent trajectories for high-stakes decision-making verification.

entry.title: Compositional Visual Planning via Inference-Time Diffusion Scaling

author.name: Yixin Zhang, Yunhao Luo, Utkarsh Aashu Mishra, Woo Chul Shin, Yongxin Chen, Danfei Xu

entry.summary: This paper proposes compositional visual planning via inference-time diffusion scaling, where long-horizon plans are composed from short segments by enforcing boundary agreement on clean data estimates (Tweedie estimates) rather than noisy intermediate states, formulated as inference on chain-structured factor graphs.

entry.title: RAPO: Expanding Exploration for LLM Agents via Retrieval-Augmented Policy Optimization

author.name: Siwei Zhang, Yun Xiong, Xi Chen, Zi'an Jia, Renhong Huang, Jiarong Xu, Jiawei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes RAPO, a retrieval-augmented policy optimization framework for LLM agents that expands exploration by incorporating fine-grained off-policy signals at the step level rather than full trajectory level.

entry.title: Evaluating Cross-Modal Reasoning Ability and Problem Characteristics with Multimodal Item Response Theory

author.name: Shunki Uebayashi, Kento Masui, Kyohei Atarashi, Han Bao, Hisashi Kashima, Naoto Inoue, Mayu Otani, Koh Takeuchi

entry.summary: Introduces M3IRT, a multimodal item response theory framework for evaluating MLLMs that decomposes model ability and item difficulty into modality-specific dimensions, identifying shortcut questions that can be solved with a single modality.

entry.title: SIGMark: Scalable In-Generation Watermark with Blind Extraction for Video Diffusion

author.name: Xinjie Zhu, Zijing Zhao, Hui Jin, Qingxiao Guo, Yilong Ma, Yunhao Wang, Xiaobing Guo, Weifeng Zhang

entry.summary: SIGMark introduces a scalable in-generation watermarking method for video diffusion models that supports blind extraction (no need for template matching), addressing the prohibitive computational costs of existing non-blind in-generation watermarking approaches.

entry.title: Estimating Visual Attribute Effects in Advertising from Observational Data: A Deepfake-Informed Double Machine Learning Approach

author.name: Yizhi Liu, Balaji Padmanabhan, Siva Viswanathan

entry.summary: Develops DICE-DML, a framework using deepfake-generated counterfactual images to disentangle visual treatment variables (like skin tone) from confounders in advertising research, enabling causal estimation of visual attribute effects on engagement.

entry.title: EvoSkill: Automated Skill Discovery for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Salaheddin Alzubi, Noah Provenzano, Jaydon Bingham, Weiyuan Chen, Tu Vu

entry.summary: Introduces EvoSkill, a self-evolving framework that automatically discovers and refines agent skills through iterative failure analysis, materializing skills as reusable workflows rather than low-level prompt/code optimizations.

entry.title: Retrievit: In-context Retrieval Capabilities of Transformers, State Space Models, and Hybrid Architectures

author.name: Georgios Pantazopoulos, Malvina Nikandrou, Ioannis Konstas, Alessandro Suglia

entry.summary: Investigates in-context retrieval capabilities of Transformers, State Space Models, and hybrid architectures on synthetic tasks (n-gram retrieval, position retrieval), finding that hybrid architectures can combine the efficiency of SSMs with retrieval strengths of Transformers.

entry.title: MedCalc-Bench Doesn't Measure What You Think: A Benchmark Audit and the Case for Open-Book Evaluation

author.name: Artus Krohn-Grimberghe

entry.summary: Audits MedCalc-Bench, a clinical calculator benchmark, finding over 20 errors in calculator implementations and showing that simple 'open-book' prompting (providing calculator specs) raises accuracy from 35% to near-perfect, challenging the benchmark's framing.

entry.title: Structured vs. Unstructured Pruning: An Exponential Gap

author.name: Davide Ferr\'e (CNRS, COATI, UniCA, I3S), Fr\'ed\'eric Giroire (I3S, COATI, UniCA), Emanuele Natale (CNRS, COATI, I3S, UniCA), Frederik Mallmann-Trenn

entry.summary: Proves an exponential gap between structured (neuron) pruning and unstructured pruning in the Strong Lottery Ticket Hypothesis, showing that neuron pruning requires exponentially more overparameterization.

entry.title: Concept Heterogeneity-aware Representation Steering

author.name: Laziz U. Abdullaev, Noelle Y. L. Wong, Ryan T. Z. Lee, Shiqi Jiang, Khoi N. M. Nguyen, Tan M. Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes viewing representation steering through optimal transport, addressing non-homogeneous concept representations in LLMs where global steering directions fail due to clustered, context-dependent structure.

entry.title: When Scaling Fails: Mitigating Audio Perception Decay of LALMs via Multi-Step Perception-Aware Reasoning

author.name: Ruixiang Mao, Xiangnan Ma, Dan Chen, Ziming Zhu, Yuan Ge, Aokai Hao, Haishu Zhao, Yifu Huo, Qing Yang, Kaiyan Chang, Xiaoqian Liu, Chenglong Wang, Qiaozhi He, Tong Xiao, Jingbo Zhu

entry.summary: Identifies that Large Audio-Language Models suffer from audio perception decay as reasoning chains lengthen—reasoning performance degrades because the model loses track of audio content. Proposes MPAR² to encourage dynamic perceptual re-engagement during reasoning.

entry.title: The Malignant Tail: Spectral Segregation of Label Noise in Over-Parameterized Networks

author.name: Zice Wang

entry.summary: Experimentally identifies the 'Malignant Tail' phenomenon where networks segregate signal into low-rank subspaces and push label noise into high-frequency orthogonal components, explaining the phase transition from benign to harmful overfitting.

entry.title: Rigidity-Aware Geometric Pretraining for Protein Design and Conformational Ensembles

author.name: Zhanghan Ni, Yanjing Li, Zeju Qiu, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Hongyu Guo, Weiyang Liu, Shengchao Liu

entry.summary: Introduces RigidSSL, a self-supervised pretraining framework for protein design that learns rigidity-aware geometric representations, jointly addressing protein geometry understanding and conformational ensemble modeling.

entry.title: Bridging Diffusion Guidance and Anderson Acceleration via Hopfield Dynamics

author.name: Kwanyoung Kim

entry.summary: Establishes a theoretical framework connecting attention-space extrapolation in diffusion models to Anderson Acceleration applied to Modern Hopfield Network dynamics, providing theoretical grounding for CFG-like techniques in attention space.

entry.title: Practical FP4 Training for Large-Scale MoE Models on Hopper GPUs

author.name: Wuyue Zhang, Chongdong Huang, Chunbo You, Cheng Gu, Fengjuan Wang, Mou Sun

entry.summary: Presents a practical FP4 training recipe for large-scale MoE models on Hopper GPUs without native 4-bit compute support, introducing direct FP8-to-FP4 quantization and achieving significant activation memory reduction.

entry.title: TrustMH-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating the Trustworthiness of Large Language Models in Mental Health

author.name: Zixin Xiong, Ziteng Wang, Haotian Fan, Xinjie Zhang, Wenxuan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes TrustMH-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM trustworthiness specifically in mental health contexts across eight pillars including reliability, crisis identification, and safety. Addresses the gap between general-purpose LLM evaluation and domain-specific mental health requirements.

entry.title: Chain of World: World Model Thinking in Latent Motion

author.name: Fuxiang Yang, Donglin Di, Lulu Tang, Xuancheng Zhang, Lei Fan, Hao Li, Chen Wei, Tonghua Su, Baorui Ma

entry.summary: Introduces CoWVLA (Chain-of-World VLA), which unifies world-model temporal reasoning with disentangled latent motion representation for embodied AI. Uses a pretrained video VAE to factorize video into structural context and latent motion codes, avoiding redundant background reconstruction.

entry.title: How to Peel with a Knife: Aligning Fine-Grained Manipulation with Human Preference

author.name: Toru Lin, Shuying Deng, Zhao-Heng Yin, Pieter Abbeel, Jitendra Malik

entry.summary: Presents a learning framework for fine-grained manipulation tasks with subjective success criteria (like peeling with a knife), using force-aware imitation learning followed by human preference-based refinement via RLHF.

entry.title: MUSE: A Run-Centric Platform for Multimodal Unified Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models

author.name: Zhongxi Wang, Yueqian Lin, Jingyang Zhang, Hai Helen Li, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: Presents MUSE, an open-source platform for multimodal safety evaluation of LLMs integrating cross-modal payload generation, multi-turn attack algorithms, and an LLM judge with a five-level safety taxonomy. Introduces dual-metric framework distinguishing hard and soft attack success rates.

entry.title: Wasserstein Proximal Policy Gradient

author.name: Zhaoyu Zhu, Shuhan Zhang, Rui Gao, Shuang Li

entry.summary: Derives Wasserstein Proximal Policy Gradient (WPPG) for continuous-action entropy-regularized RL through operator splitting, enabling use with implicit stochastic policies without evaluating log densities. Establishes global linear convergence rate.

entry.title: SaFeR-ToolKit: Structured Reasoning via Virtual Tool Calling for Multimodal Safety

author.name: Zixuan Xu, Tiancheng He, Huahui Yi, Kun Wang, Xi Chen, Gongli Xi, Qiankun Li, Kang Li, Yang Liu, Zhigang Zeng

entry.summary: Proposes SaFeR-ToolKit, which formalizes VLM safety decision-making as a checkable protocol with typed tool traces and trains using a three-stage curriculum (SFT→DPO→GRPO). Directly supervises tool usage beyond answer-level feedback.

entry.title: HomeAdam: Adam and AdamW Algorithms Sometimes Go Home to Obtain Better Provable Generalization

author.name: Feihu Huang, Guanyi Zhang, Songcan Chen

entry.summary: Proposes HomeAdam, proving that Adam/AdamW variants without square roots achieve O(ρ^{-2T}/N) generalization error that can improve to O(1/N) matching SGD's rate. Provides first theoretical explanation for improved generalization of Adam variants.

entry.title: Less Noise, Same Certificate: Retain Sensitivity for Unlearning

author.name: Carolin Heinzler, Kasra Malihi, Amartya Sanyal

entry.summary: Shows that certified machine unlearning can use less noise than differential privacy by introducing 'retain sensitivity' - recognizing that unlearning doesn't need to protect retained data privacy, just match retraining output distribution.

entry.title: Adaptive Methods Are Preferable in High Privacy Settings: An SDE Perspective

author.name: Enea Monzio Compagnoni, Alessandro Stanghellini, Rustem Islamov, Aurelien Lucchi, Anastasiia Koloskova

entry.summary: Provides SDE-based analysis showing DP-SignSGD outperforms DP-SGD in high-privacy regimes under fixed hyperparameters, with privacy-utility trade-off of O(1/ε) vs O(1/ε²), offering first SDE-based analysis of private optimizers.

entry.title: Low-Degree Method Fails to Predict Robust Subspace Recovery

author.name: He Jia, Aravindan Vijayaraghavan

entry.summary: Identifies a natural hypothesis testing problem that is polynomial-time solvable but where the low-degree polynomial method fails to predict computational tractability, challenging the low-degree conjecture.

entry.title: DREAM: Where Visual Understanding Meets Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Chao Li, Tianhong Li, Sai Vidyaranya Nuthalapati, Hong-You Chen, Satya Narayan Shukla, Yonghuan Yang, Jun Xiao, Xiangjun Fan, Aashu Singh, Dina Katabi, Shlok Kumar Mishra

entry.summary: DREAM unifies visual representation learning and text-to-image generation in a single model using masking warmup (progressive masking schedule) and semantically aligned decoding, jointly optimizing discriminative and generative objectives.

entry.title: MoD-DPO: Towards Mitigating Cross-modal Hallucinations in Omni LLMs using Modality Decoupled Preference Optimization

author.name: Ashutosh Chaubey, Jiacheng Pang, Mohammad Soleymani

entry.summary: Proposes MoD-DPO, a modality-decoupled direct preference optimization framework for reducing cross-modal hallucinations in omni-modal LLMs through modality-aware regularization.

entry.title: LoGeR: Long-Context Geometric Reconstruction with Hybrid Memory

author.name: Junyi Zhang, Charles Herrmann, Junhwa Hur, Chen Sun, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Forrester Cole, Trevor Darrell, Deqing Sun

entry.summary: LoGeR scales dense 3D reconstruction to extremely long video sequences using a hybrid memory module combining parametric Test-Time Training memory with bidirectional intra-chunk processing, avoiding post-optimization.

entry.title: Think, But Don't Overthink: Reproducing Recursive Language Models

author.name: Daren Wang

entry.summary: Reproduces and extends Recursive Language Models (RLMs) framework, investigating the effect of scaling recursion depth. Discovers that deeper recursion causes models to 'overthink,' degrading performance—depth-1 helps but depth-2 hurts across benchmarks with DeepSeek v3.2 and Kimi K2.

entry.title: Graph-GRPO: Stabilizing Multi-Agent Topology Learning via Group Relative Policy Optimization

author.name: Yueyang Cang, Xiaoteng Zhang, Erlu Zhao, Zehua Ji, Yuhang Liu, Yuchen He, Zhiyuan Ning, Chen Yijun, Wenge Que, Li Shi

entry.summary: Proposes Graph-GRPO, applying Group Relative Policy Optimization to optimize communication topologies in LLM-based multi-agent systems. Addresses gradient variance and credit assignment problems in topology learning with relative reward comparisons.

entry.title: MaBERT:A Padding Safe Interleaved Transformer Mamba Hybrid Encoder for Efficient Extended Context Masked Language Modeling

author.name: Jinwoong Kim, Sangjin Park

entry.summary: Proposes MaBERT, a hybrid Transformer-Mamba encoder that interleaves self-attention layers with Mamba SSM layers for efficient long-context masked language modeling, introducing padding-safe masking to prevent state contamination in variable-length batches.

entry.title: Code2Math: Can Your Code Agent Effectively Evolve Math Problems Through Exploration?

author.name: Dadi Guo, Yuejin Xie, Qingyu Liu, Jiayu Liu, Zhiyuan Fan, Qihan Ren, Shuai Shao, Tianyi Zhou, Dongrui Liu, Yi R. Fung

entry.summary: Investigates whether code agents can autonomously evolve math problems into more complex variations, using a multi-agent framework that validates solvability and increased difficulty. Demonstrates code execution as a scalable environment for mathematical experimentation.

entry.title: TruckDrive: Long-Range Autonomous Highway Driving Dataset

author.name: Filippo Ghilotti, Edoardo Palladin, Samuel Brucker, Adam Sigal, Mario Bijelic, Felix Heide

entry.summary: Introduces TruckDrive, a highway-scale multimodal driving dataset for long-range sensing (hundreds of meters) captured with FMCW LiDARs, cameras, and 4D radars, addressing the gap that existing datasets only cover ~100m range.

entry.title: ModalPatch: A Plug-and-Play Module for Robust Multi-Modal 3D Object Detection under Modality Drop

author.name: Shuangzhi Li, Lei Ma, Xingyu Li

entry.summary: Introduces ModalPatch, a plug-and-play module for robust 3D object detection under arbitrary modality-drop scenarios (sensor failures), enabling detection even during simultaneous LiDAR and camera dropout without retraining.

entry.title: Generalizable Knowledge Distillation from Vision Foundation Models for Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Chonghua Lv, Dong Zhao, Shuang Wang, Dou Quan, Ning Huyan, Nicu Sebe, Zhun Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes GKD (Generalizable Knowledge Distillation) for semantic segmentation, a multi-stage framework that explicitly preserves the out-of-domain generalization capabilities of vision foundation models during distillation.

entry.title: From "What" to "How": Constrained Reasoning for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Ruxue Yan, Xubo Liu, Wenya Guo, Zhengkun Zhang, Ying Zhang, Xiaojie Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes CoR-Painter, introducing constrained reasoning for autoregressive image generation that shifts from 'what to draw' to 'how to draw' by deriving spatial constraints before generation, addressing object overlap issues.

entry.title: VSearcher: Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agent via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ruiyang Zhang, Qianguo Sun, Chao Song, Yiyan Qi, Zhedong Zheng

entry.summary: VSearcher converts a static multimodal model into a multimodal search agent capable of long-horizon, multi-turn tool use (text search, image search, web browsing) in real-world web environments using reinforcement learning. This bridges the gap between strong perceptual capabilities of multimodal models and their inability to access up-to-date web information.

entry.title: GloPath: An Entity-Centric Foundation Model for Glomerular Lesion Assessment and Clinicopathological Insights

author.name: Qiming He, Jing Li, Tian Guan, Yifei Ma, Zimo Zhao, Yanxia Wang, Hongjing Chen, Yingming Xu, Shuang Ge, Yexing Zhang, Yizhi Wang, Xinrui Chen, Lianghui Zhu, Yiqing Liu, Qingxia Hou, Shuyan Zhao, Xiaoqin Wang, Lili Ma, Peizhen Hu, Qiang Huang, Zihan Wang, Zhiyuan Shen, Junru Cheng, Siqi Zeng, Jiurun Chen, Zhen Song, Chao He, Zhe Wang, Yonghong He

entry.summary: GloPath is a foundation model for glomerular pathology trained on over 1M glomeruli from 14K renal biopsies using multi-scale self-supervised learning, benchmarked across 52 tasks including lesion recognition, grading, few-shot classification, and cross-modality diagnosis.

entry.title: TRACE: Task-Adaptive Reasoning and Representation Learning for Universal Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Xiangzhao Hao, Shijie Wang, Tianyu Yang, Tianyue Wang, Haiyun Guo, JinQiao Wang

entry.summary: TRACE introduces a framework for universal multimodal retrieval that unifies generative chain-of-thought reasoning with discriminative representation learning, generating structured reasoning about queries before producing compressed embeddings.

entry.title: Rhythm: Learning Interactive Whole-Body Control for Dual Humanoids

author.name: Hongjin Chen, Wei Zhang, Pengfei Li, Shihao Ma, Ke Ma, Yujie Jin, Zijun Xu, Xiaohui Wang, Yupeng Zheng, Zining Wang, Jieru Zhao, Yilun Chen, Wenchao Ding

entry.summary: Rhythm is the first framework enabling real-world deployment of dual-humanoid systems for complex physically plausible interactions, integrating interaction-aware motion retargeting, coupled control, and interaction synthesis.

entry.title: HoMMI: Learning Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation from Human Demonstrations

author.name: Xiaomeng Xu, Jisang Park, Han Zhang, Eric Cousineau, Aditya Bhat, Jose Barreiros, Dian Wang, Shuran Song

entry.summary: HoMMI enables learning whole-body mobile manipulation policies directly from robot-free human demonstrations by augmenting UMI interfaces with egocentric sensing. The framework addresses the human-to-robot embodiment gap through cross-embodiment hand-eye policy design with embodiment-agnostic visual representations.

entry.title: I'm confused by the change in the METR trend

author.name: Expertium

entry.summary: Analyzes the METR benchmark trend showing AI task completion doubling time changed significantly for models released in 2024 and later. Uses statistical methods (BIC, cross-validation) to confirm the piecewise linear fit is robust and not a random fluke, finding the trend change is real.

entry.title: Beyond Task Completion: Revealing Corrupt Success in LLM Agents through Procedure-Aware Evaluation

author.name: Hongliu Cao, Ilias Driouich, Eoin Thomas

entry.summary: Introduces Procedure-Aware Evaluation (PAE) for LLM agents that evaluates not just task completion but how tasks are completed, exposing 'corrupt success' through multi-dimensional gating across utility, efficiency, interaction quality, and procedural integrity.

entry.title: A Neuropsychologically Grounded Evaluation of LLM Cognitive Abilities

author.name: Faiz Ghifari Haznitrama, Faeyza Rishad Ardi, Alice Oh

entry.summary: Introduces NeuroCognition benchmark grounded in three neuropsychological tests (Raven's Matrices, Spatial Working Memory, Wisconsin Card Sorting) to probe foundational cognitive abilities in LLMs. Finds models perform well on text but degrade significantly on non-verbal analogs.

entry.title: No Memorization, No Detection: Output Distribution-Based Contamination Detection in Small Language Models

author.name: Omer Sela

entry.summary: Studies contamination detection via output distribution (CDD) in small language models, finding it fails when fine-tuning doesn't produce verbatim memorization (e.g., with LoRA), only working when training capacity induces memorization.

entry.title: Inherited Goal Drift: Contextual Pressure Can Undermine Agentic Goals

author.name: Achyutha Menon, Magnus Saebo, Tyler Crosse, Spencer Gibson, Eyon Jang, Diogo Cruz

entry.summary: Studies goal drift in LLM agents in a stock-trading environment, finding state-of-the-art models are largely robust to adversarial pressure but this robustness is brittle - breaking when models inherit goals from system prompts of other models.

entry.title: ATPO: Adaptive Tree Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Medical Dialogue

author.name: Ruike Cao, Shaojie Bai, Fugen Yao, Liang Dong, Jian Xu, Li Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes ATPO (Adaptive Tree Policy Optimization) for multi-turn medical dialogue, formulated as a Hierarchical MDP with uncertainty-aware adaptive rollout budget allocation for training LLMs to conduct diagnostic conversations.

entry.title: CUDABench: Benchmarking LLMs for Text-to-CUDA Generation

author.name: Jiace Zhu, Wentao Chen, Qi Fan, Zhixing Ren, Junying Wu, Xing Zhe Chai, Chotiwit Rungrueangwutthinon, Yehan Ma, An Zou

entry.summary: Introduces CUDABench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLM text-to-CUDA generation capabilities across diverse application domains including AI, scientific computing, and data analysis.

entry.title: Universal Conceptual Structure in Neural Translation: Probing NLLB-200's Multilingual Geometry

author.name: Kyle Elliott Mathewson

entry.summary: Probes Meta's NLLB-200 translation model to investigate whether it learns language-universal conceptual representations. Finds embedding distances correlate with phylogenetic distances, suggesting the model has implicitly learned genealogical structure of human languages.

entry.title: Characterizing VLA Models: Identifying the Action Generation Bottleneck for Edge AI Architectures

author.name: Manoj Vishwanathan, Suvinay Subramanian, Anand Raghunathan

entry.summary: Characterizes Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model performance on edge hardware (Nvidia Jetson Orin/Thor), identifying that 75% of latency comes from memory-bound action generation. Projects hardware requirements for 100B parameter models.

entry.title: How Controllable Are Large Language Models? A Unified Evaluation across Behavioral Granularities

author.name: Ziwen Xu, Kewei Xu, Haoming Xu, Haiwen Hong, Longtao Huang, Hui Xue, Ningyu Zhang, Yongliang Shen, Guozhou Zheng, Huajun Chen, Shumin Deng

entry.summary: Introduces SteerEval, a hierarchical benchmark for evaluating LLM controllability across language features, sentiment, and personality at three specification levels, revealing that control degrades at finer-grained levels.

entry.title: Eliciting Numerical Predictive Distributions of LLMs Without Autoregression

author.name: Julianna Piskorz, Katarzyna Kobalczyk, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM predictive distributions for numerical tasks can be recovered without autoregressive generation, training regression probes on hidden states to predict statistical functionals like mean, median, and quantiles.

entry.title: On the Expressive Power of Transformers for Maxout Networks and Continuous Piecewise Linear Functions

author.name: Linyan Gu, Lihua Yang, Feng Zhou

entry.summary: Studies the expressive power of Transformer architectures by establishing explicit approximation of maxout networks by Transformers, showing Transformers inherit universal approximation capabilities of ReLU networks. Develops a framework to analyze approximation of continuous piecewise linear functions.

entry.title: Geometry-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Multi-view Consistent 3D Scene Editing

author.name: Jiyuan Wang, Chunyu Lin, Lei Sun, Zhi Cao, Yuyang Yin, Lang Nie, Zhenlong Yuan, Xiangxiang Chu, Yunchao Wei, Kang Liao, Guosheng Lin

entry.summary: Proposes RL3DEdit, a single-pass 3D scene editing framework that uses reinforcement learning with rewards from the VGGT 3D foundation model to achieve multi-view consistent editing. Leverages the insight that verifying 3D consistency is easier than generating it.

entry.title: ParEVO: Synthesizing Code for Irregular Data: High-Performance Parallelism through Agentic Evolution

author.name: Liu Yang, Zeyu Nie, Andrew Liu, Felix Zou, Deniz Altinb\"uken, Amir Yazdanbakhsh, Quanquan C. Liu

entry.summary: Introduces ParEVO, a framework for synthesizing high-performance parallel algorithms for irregular data structures using LLM-based agentic evolution. Includes the Parlay-Instruct Corpus with 13,800+ examples for parallel programming.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Agent Collaborative Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhixia Zhang, Zixuan Huang, Xin Xia, Deqing Wang, Fuzhen Zhuang, Shuai Ma, Ning Ding, Yaodong Yang, Jianxin Li, Yikun Ban

entry.summary: Introduces HACRL, a paradigm where heterogeneous RL agents share verified rollouts during training for mutual improvement while executing independently at inference. Proposes HACPO algorithm enabling bidirectional learning unlike one-directional distillation.

entry.title: Learning in Markov Decision Processes with Exogenous Dynamics

author.name: Davide Maran, Davide Salaorni, Marcello Restelli

entry.summary: Studies MDPs with exogenous state components whose transitions are independent of agent actions, showing that exploiting this structure yields significantly improved regret bounds where only exogenous state space size appears in leading terms.

entry.title: The Alignment Flywheel: A Governance-Centric Hybrid MAS for Architecture-Agnostic Safety

author.name: Elias Malomgr\'e, Pieter Simoens

entry.summary: Formalizes the 'Alignment Flywheel' as a governance-centric hybrid multi-agent system architecture that decouples decision generation from safety governance, with a Safety Oracle providing signals separate from the decision Proposer.

entry.title: Generalized Bayes for Causal Inference

author.name: Emil Javurek, Dennis Frauen, Yuxin Wang, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: Proposes a generalized Bayesian framework for causal inference that avoids explicit likelihood modeling, placing priors directly on causal estimands and updating via identification-driven loss functions.

entry.title: TAO-Attack: Toward Advanced Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attacks for Large Language Models

author.name: Zhi Xu, Jiaqi Li, Xiaotong Zhang, Hong Yu, Han Liu

entry.summary: Proposes TAO-Attack, an optimization-based jailbreak method using a two-stage loss function that first suppresses refusals then penalizes pseudo-harmful outputs, improving attack success rates against aligned LLMs.

entry.title: Cultural Counterfactuals: Evaluating Cultural Biases in Large Vision-Language Models with Counterfactual Examples

author.name: Phillip Howard, Xin Su, Kathleen C. Fraser

entry.summary: Introduces a dataset and methodology for evaluating cultural biases in large vision-language models using counterfactual examples, addressing biases related to religion and socioeconomic status that cannot be discerned from appearance alone.

entry.title: On Discriminative vs. Generative classifiers: Rethinking MLLMs for Action Understanding

author.name: Zhanzhong Pang, Dibyadip Chatterjee, Fadime Sener, Angela Yao

entry.summary: Compares generative vs. discriminative classification approaches with MLLMs for action understanding, finding discriminative classifiers superior in accuracy and efficiency. Designs strategies to bridge the performance gap between approaches.

entry.title: VisionCreator: A Native Visual-Generation Agentic Model with Understanding, Thinking, Planning and Creation

author.name: Jinxiang Lai, Zexin Lu, Jiajun He, Rongwei Quan, Wenzhe Zhao, Qinyu Yang, Qi Chen, Qin Lin, Chuyue Li, Tao Gao, Yuhao Shan, Shuai Shao, Song Guo, Qinglin Lu

entry.summary: Proposes VisionCreator, a native visual-generation agentic model unifying Understanding, Thinking, Planning, and Creation within an end-to-end framework, using metacognition-based data generation for training creation trajectories.

entry.title: MiM-DiT: MoE in MoE with Diffusion Transformers for All-in-One Image Restoration

author.name: Lingshun Kong, Jiawei Zhang, Zhengpeng Duan, Xiaohe Wu, Yueqi Yang, Xiaotao Wang, Dongqing Zou, Lei Lei, Jinshan Pan

entry.summary: Proposes MiM-DiT, a dual-level Mixture-of-Experts architecture integrated with pretrained diffusion models for all-in-one image restoration, with Inter-MoE for degradation types and Intra-MoE for fine-grained variations.

entry.title: Seeing Clearly without Training: Mitigating Hallucinations in Multimodal LLMs for Remote Sensing

author.name: Yi Liu, Jing Zhang, Di Wang, Xiaoyu Tian, Haonan Guo, Bo Du

entry.summary: Introduces RSHBench for diagnosing hallucinations in MLLMs for remote sensing VQA, and proposes RADAR, a training-free inference method using intrinsic attention for progressive localization and fine-grained reasoning.

entry.title: NOVA: Sparse Control, Dense Synthesis for Pair-Free Video Editing

author.name: Tianlin Pan, Jiayi Dai, Chenpu Yuan, Zhengyao Lv, Binxin Yang, Hubery Yin, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Caifeng Shan, Chenyang Si

entry.summary: NOVA introduces a pair-free video editing framework using sparse control (user-edited keyframes) and dense synthesis (continuous motion/texture incorporation), eliminating the need for large-scale paired training datasets that are a critical bottleneck for video editing models.

entry.title: Kling-MotionControl Technical Report

author.name: Kling Team, Jialu Chen, Yikang Ding, Zhixue Fang, Kun Gai, Kang He, Xu He, Jingyun Hua, Mingming Lao, Xiaohan Li, Hui Liu, Jiwen Liu, Xiaoqiang Liu, Fan Shi, Xiaoyu Shi, Peiqin Sun, Songlin Tang, Pengfei Wan, Tiancheng Wen, Zhiyong Wu, Haoxian Zhang, Runze Zhao, Yuanxing Zhang, Yan Zhou

entry.summary: Kling-MotionControl is a unified DiT-based framework for holistic character animation that handles body, face, and hands via a divide-and-conquer strategy with heterogeneous motion representations, enabling robust cross-identity generalization.

entry.title: COP-GEN: Latent Diffusion Transformer for Copernicus Earth Observation Data -- Generation Stochastic by Design

author.name: Miguel Espinosa, Eva Gmelich Meijling, Valerio Marsocci, Elliot J. Crowley, Mikolaj Czerkawski

entry.summary: COP-GEN is a multimodal latent diffusion transformer for modeling the joint distribution of heterogeneous Earth observation data (optical, radar, elevation, land-cover), addressing the non-injective nature of cross-sensor relationships that deterministic models collapse on.

entry.title: A Dynamical Theory of Sequential Retrieval in Input-Driven Hopfield Networks

author.name: Simone Betteti, Giacomo Baggio, Sandro Zampieri

entry.summary: This paper provides a dynamical theory of sequential retrieval in input-driven Hopfield networks, offering theoretical foundations for how associative memory models perform sequential retrieval and multi-memory integration, bridging to understanding ML reasoning.

entry.title: Current activation oracles are hard to use

author.name: aryaj

entry.summary: Reports negative results from MATS 9.0 on activation oracles—models finetuned to answer questions about another model's activations. Found them difficult to use for safety-relevant tasks, with 49.4% of responses being generic/vague and poor generalization beyond training distribution.

entry.title: NeuroProlog: Multi-Task Fine-Tuning for Neurosymbolic Mathematical Reasoning via the Cocktail Effect

author.name: Pratibha Zunjare, Michael Hsiao

entry.summary: Presents NeuroProlog, a neurosymbolic framework that compiles math word problems into executable Prolog programs with formal verification, using a multi-task 'Cocktail' training strategy that jointly optimizes formula translation, program synthesis, and answer alignment.

entry.title: LiveAgentBench: Comprehensive Benchmarking of Agentic Systems Across 104 Real-World Challenges

author.name: Hao Li, Huan Wang, Jinjie Gu, Wenjie Wang, Chenyi Zhuang, Sikang Bian

entry.summary: Presents LiveAgentBench, a benchmark with 104 real-world scenarios sourced from social media and real products for evaluating AI agents, using a Social Perception-Driven Data Generation method to ensure task relevance and complexity.

entry.title: RxnNano:Training Compact LLMs for Chemical Reaction and Retrosynthesis Prediction via Hierarchical Curriculum Learning

author.name: Ran Li, Shimin Di, Haowei LI, Luanshi Bu, Jiachuan Wang, Wangze Ni, Lei Chen

entry.summary: Proposes RxnNano, training compact LLMs for chemical reaction and retrosynthesis prediction using hierarchical curriculum learning with a Latent Chemical Consistency objective that models reactions as movements on a continuous chemical manifold.

entry.title: Forecasting as Rendering: A 2D Gaussian Splatting Framework for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yixin Wang, Yifan Hu, Peiyuan Liu, Naiqi Li, Dai Tao, Shu-Tao Xia

entry.summary: Introduces TimeGS, a novel framework that recasts time series forecasting as 2D Gaussian splatting, addressing topological mismatch and fixed-resolution limitations of existing period-phase representation methods.

entry.title: Talking with Verifiers: Automatic Specification Generation for Neural Network Verification

author.name: Yizhak Y. Elboher, Reuven Peleg, Zhouxing Shi, Guy Katz, Jan K\v{r}et\'insk\'y

entry.summary: Introduces a novel component for neural network verification pipelines that automatically generates high-level semantic specifications from natural language, bridging the gap between human-understandable correctness requirements and low-level verification constraints.

entry.title: Manifold Aware Denoising Score Matching (MAD)

author.name: Alona Levy-Jurgenson, Alvaro Prat, James Cuin, Yee Whye Teh

entry.summary: Proposes Manifold Aware Denoising (MAD) score matching that decomposes the score function into a known base component encoding manifold information and a learned remainder, reducing the burden of implicitly learning the manifold while maintaining computational efficiency.

entry.title: Through the Lens of Contrast: Self-Improving Visual Reasoning in VLMs

author.name: Zhiyu Pan, Yizheng Wu, Jiashen Hua, Junyi Feng, Shaotian Yan, Bing Deng, Zhiguo Cao, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: Proposes VC-STaR, which uses visual contrast (comparing similar images with synonymous questions) to help VLMs identify relevant visual cues more precisely, reducing visual hallucinations in self-improving reasoning paths.

entry.title: Efficient Self-Evaluation for Diffusion Language Models via Sequence Regeneration

author.name: Linhao Zhong, Linyu Wu, Wen Wang, Yuling Xi, Chenchen Jing, Jiaheng Zhang, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: Proposes DiSE, a self-evaluation method for diffusion language models that quantifies confidence by computing regeneration probability of generated tokens, enabling likelihood estimation and uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: From Complex Dynamics to DynFormer: Rethinking Transformers for PDEs

author.name: Pengyu Lai, Yixiao Chen, Dewu Yang, Rui Wang, Feng Wang, Hui Xu

entry.summary: Proposes DynFormer, a dynamics-informed neural operator for PDEs that rethinks transformers through the lens of complex dynamics, separating smooth large-scale dynamics from high-frequency fluctuations rather than treating all spatial points as uniform tokens.

entry.title: APRES: An Agentic Paper Revision and Evaluation System

author.name: Bingchen Zhao, Jenny Zhang, Chenxi Whitehouse, Minqi Jiang, Michael Shvartsman, Abhishek Charnalia, Despoina Magka, Tatiana Shavrina, Derek Dunfield, Oisin Mac Aodha, Yoram Bachrach

entry.summary: Introduces APRES, an LLM-powered system that discovers evaluation rubrics predictive of citation counts and uses them to automatically revise scientific paper text. Combines automated peer review with paper revision in an agentic framework.

entry.title: Tether: Autonomous Functional Play with Correspondence-Driven Trajectory Warping

author.name: William Liang, Sam Wang, Hung-Ju Wang, Osbert Bastani, Yecheng Jason Ma, Dinesh Jayaraman

entry.summary: Introduces Tether, a method for autonomous robot functional play that warps actions from a small set of demonstrations using semantic keypoint correspondences. Achieves data-efficient policy transfer with ≤10 demonstrations.

entry.title: Same Error, Different Function: The Optimizer as an Implicit Prior in Financial Time Series

author.name: Federico Vittorio Cortesi, Giuseppe Iannone, Giulia Crippa, Tomaso Poggio, Pierfrancesco Beneventano

entry.summary: Shows that in financial time series forecasting, different model-training pipelines achieving identical test loss learn qualitatively different functions, with optimizer choice reshaping response profiles. These differences lead to 3x turnover dispersion in volatility-ranked portfolios.

entry.title: An Empirical Analysis of Calibration and Selective Prediction in Multimodal Clinical Condition Classification

author.name: L. Juli\'an Lechuga L\'opez, Farah E. Shamout, Tim G. J. Rudner

entry.summary: Empirically evaluates uncertainty-based selective prediction in multilabel clinical classification using multimodal ICU data, finding that selective prediction can substantially degrade performance due to severe class-dependent miscalibration.

entry.title: Fisher-Geometric Diffusion in Stochastic Gradient Descent: Optimal Rates, Oracle Complexity, and Information-Theoretic Limits

author.name: Daniel Zantedeschi, Kumar Muthuraman

entry.summary: Develops Fisher-geometric theory of SGD where mini-batch noise is treated as intrinsic loss-induced matrix rather than exogenous scalar, deriving convergence rates and minimax optimality bounds through SDE analysis.

entry.title: From Solver to Tutor: Evaluating the Pedagogical Intelligence of LLMs with KMP-Bench

author.name: Weikang Shi, Houxing Ren, Junting Pan, Aojun Zhou, Ke Wang, Zimu Lu, Yunqiao Yang, Yuxuan Hu, Linda Wei, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: Introduces KMP-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs as K-8 math tutors from two perspectives: holistic pedagogical dialogue capabilities and granular foundational tutoring skills assessment.

entry.title: Toward Early Quality Assessment of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Huanlei Guo, Hongxin Wei, Bingyi Jing

entry.summary: Introduces Probe-Select, a plug-in module that evaluates text-to-image generation quality early in the denoising process by analyzing intermediate activations, reducing computational waste in generate-then-select pipelines.

entry.title: CamDirector: Towards Long-Term Coherent Video Trajectory Editing

author.name: Zhihao Shi, Kejia Yin, Weilin Wan, Yuhongze Zhou, Yuanhao Yu, Xinxin Zuo, Qiang Sun, Juwei Lu

entry.summary: Introduces CamDirector for long-term coherent video trajectory editing, using a hybrid warping scheme that aggregates information across the entire source video via a world cache for static regions and mesh-based rendering for dynamic content.

entry.title: SemGS: Feed-Forward Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting from Sparse Views for Generalizable Scene Understanding

author.name: Sheng Ye, Zhen-Hui Dong, Ruoyu Fan, Tian Lv, Yong-Jin Liu

entry.summary: Proposes SemGS, a feed-forward framework for generalizable semantic 3D Gaussian splatting from sparse views using dual-branch architecture for color and semantic features with shared shallow CNN layers.

entry.title: ATD: Improved Transformer with Adaptive Token Dictionary for Image Restoration

author.name: Leheng Zhang, Wei Long, Yawei Li, Xingyu Zhou, Xiaorui Zhao, Shuhang Gu

entry.summary: Proposes Adaptive Token Dictionary (ATD), a transformer architecture for image restoration that enables global dependency modeling with linear complexity through a learnable token dictionary that summarizes key patterns.

entry.title: Gated Differential Linear Attention: A Linear-Time Decoder for High-Fidelity Medical Segmentation

author.name: Hongbo Zheng, Afshin Bozorgpour, Dorit Merhof, Minjia Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces PVT-GDLA, a decoder with Gated Differential Linear Attention for medical image segmentation that achieves sharp long-range dependencies at O(N) complexity by computing and subtracting two kernelized attention paths.

entry.title: 3D-DRES: Detailed 3D Referring Expression Segmentation

author.name: Qi Chen, Changli Wu, Jiayi Ji, Yiwei Ma, Liujuan Cao

entry.summary: 3D-DRES introduces a new task of detailed 3D referring expression segmentation with phrase-to-instance mapping, along with DetailRefer, a dataset of 54K descriptions across 11K objects with explicit phrase-instance annotations for fine-grained 3D vision-language understanding.

entry.title: Specificity-aware reinforcement learning for fine-grained open-world classification

author.name: Samuele Angheben, Davide Berasi, Alessandro Conti, Elisa Ricci, Yiming Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes specificity-aware reinforcement learning to steer reasoning LMMs toward predictions that are both correct and specific in fine-grained open-world classification, addressing the tendency of models to produce overly generic predictions.

entry.title: DuoMo: Dual Motion Diffusion for World-Space Human Reconstruction

author.name: Yufu Wang, Evonne Ng, Soyong Shin, Rawal Khirodkar, Yuan Dong, Zhaoen Su, Jinhyung Park, Kris Kitani, Alexander Richard, Fabian Prada, Michael Zollhofer
