author.name: Youyang Du (1 and 2), Junqiu Zhu (1), Zheng Zeng (3), Lu Wang (1), Lingqi Yan (2) ((1) Shandong University, (2) Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, (3) University of California, Santa Barbara)

entry.summary: NIST presents a neural post-processing approach that produces tessellated geometry visual effects while rendering only low-polygon meshes, using normal discrepancy as a cue for silhouette refinement with progressive image-space contour deformation.

entry.title: Fourier Angle Alignment for Oriented Object Detection in Remote Sensing

author.name: Changyu Gu, Linwei Chen, Lin Gu, Ying Fu

entry.summary: Introduces Fourier Angle Alignment for oriented object detection in remote sensing, analyzing angle information through frequency spectrum and aligning feature directions. Proposes plug-and-play FAAFusion and FAA Head modules.

entry.title: FluoCLIP: Stain-Aware Focus Quality Assessment in Fluorescence Microscopy

author.name: Hyejin Park, Jiwon Yoon, Sumin Park, Suree Kim, Sinae Jang, Eunsoo Lee, Dongmin Kang and Dongbo Min

entry.summary: FluoCLIP introduces stain-aware focus quality assessment for fluorescence microscopy, demonstrating that focus behavior varies across staining types and proposing a CLIP-based model with the FluoMix dataset for stain-conditioned assessment.

entry.title: Polarization Uncertainty-Guided Diffusion Model for Color Polarization Image Demosaicking

author.name: Chenggong Li, Yidong Luo, Junchao Zhang, Degui Yang

entry.summary: Introduces diffusion prior from text-to-image models for color polarization image demosaicking, addressing the challenge of reconstructing polarization characteristics (DOP, AOP) under limited training data.

entry.title: Bandwidth-adaptive Cloud-Assisted 360-Degree 3D Perception for Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Faisal Hawladera, Rui Meireles, Gamal Elghazaly, Ana Aguiar, Rapha\"el Frank

entry.summary: Proposes a V2X cloud-offloading approach for autonomous driving that dynamically splits transformer-based BEV 3D object detection between vehicle and cloud based on bandwidth. Addresses latency vs. compute tradeoffs in urban settings.

entry.title: DACESR: Degradation-Aware Conditional Embedding for Real-World Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Xiaoyan Lei, Wenlong Zhang, Biao Luo, Hui Liang, Weifeng Cao, Qiuting Lin

entry.summary: Proposes DACESR for real-world image super-resolution that uses a degradation-aware embedding from a fine-tuned Recognize Anything Model. Addresses limitations of multimodal models on degraded images through a degradation selection strategy.

entry.title: SHINE: Sequential Hierarchical Integration Network for EEG and MEG

author.name: Xiran Xu, Yujie Yan, Xihong Wu, and Jing Chen

entry.summary: Introduces SHINE network for reconstructing speech signals from MEG brain recordings, combining sequential hierarchical integration with auxiliary speech envelope and Mel spectrogram reconstruction.

entry.title: SongSong: A Time Phonograph for Chinese SongCi Music from Thousand of Years Away

author.name: Jiajia Li, Jiliang Hu, Ziyi Pan, Chong Chen, Zuchao Li, Ping Wang, Lefei Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SongSong, the first music generation model for restoring ancient Chinese SongCi music, along with OpenSongSong dataset featuring 29.9 hours of SongCi compositions.

entry.title: Artificial Agency Program: Curiosity, compression, and communication in agents

author.name: Richard Csaky

entry.summary: Presents the Artificial Agency Program, a position paper and research agenda for building AI as resource-bounded agents driven by curiosity-as-learning-progress. Proposes unifying predictive compression, intrinsic motivation, empowerment, and language as selective information bottlenecks.

entry.title: End-to-end Differentiable Calibration and Reconstruction for Optical Particle Detectors

author.name: Omar Alterkait, C\'esar Jes\'us-Valls, Ryo Matsumoto, Patrick de Perio, and Kazuhiro Terao

entry.summary: Presents the first end-to-end differentiable optical particle detector simulator for neutrino physics, enabling simultaneous calibration and reconstruction through gradient-based optimization rather than treating them as separate problems.

entry.title: What You Read is What You Classify: Highlighting Attributions to Text and Text-Like Inputs

author.name: Daniel S. Berman, Brian Merritt, Stanley Ta, Dana Udwin, Amanda Ernlund, Jeremy Ratcliff, Vijay Narayan

entry.summary: Proposes a mask-based explainable AI method for token-based classifiers that generalizes image-based attribution to text by training an Explainer network to create masks highlighting classification-relevant tokens.

entry.title: Learning Flexible Job Shop Scheduling under Limited Buffers and Material Kitting Constraints

author.name: Shishun Zhang, Juzhan Xu, Yidan Fan, Chenyang Zhu, Ruizhen Hu, Yongjun Wang, Kai Xu

entry.summary: Studies flexible job shop scheduling with limited buffers and material kitting constraints using deep RL with heterogeneous graph networks, addressing practical manufacturing constraints often ignored in academic FJSP formulations.

entry.title: Resilient Strategies for Stochastic Systems: How Much Does It Take to Break a Winning Strategy?

author.name: Kush Grover, Markel Zubia, Debraj Chakraborty, Muqsit Azeem, Nils Jansen and Jan Kretinsky

entry.summary: Studies resilient strategies in stochastic systems (MDPs and stochastic games), analyzing how robust agent strategies are against disturbances that can flip decisions, extending resilience concepts to the stochastic setting with reachability and safety objectives.

entry.title: An Efficient Unsupervised Federated Learning Approach for Anomaly Detection in Heterogeneous IoT Networks

author.name: Mohsen Tajgardan, Atena Shiranzaei, Mahdi Rabbani, Reza Khoshkangini, Mahtab Jamali

entry.summary: Proposes an unsupervised federated learning approach for anomaly detection across heterogeneous IoT networks, addressing feature heterogeneity across devices with different capabilities and data formats.

entry.title: Global Interpretability via Automated Preprocessing: A Framework Inspired by Psychiatric Questionnaires

author.name: Eric V. Strobl

entry.summary: Proposes a framework inspired by psychiatric questionnaires that decouples nonlinear preprocessing from linear prediction to achieve global interpretability. The approach stabilizes questionnaire item values through a baseline preprocessing module before applying a linear mapping to predict future symptom severity.

entry.title: ECAM: A Contrastive Learning Approach to Avoid Environmental Collision in Trajectory Forecasting

author.name: Giacomo Rosin, Muhammad Rameez Ur Rahman, Sebastiano Vascon

entry.summary: Introduces ECAM, a contrastive learning module that enhances trajectory forecasting models' ability to avoid environmental collisions. Can be integrated as a plug-in module into existing trajectory prediction models.

entry.title: Now You See Me: Designing Responsible AI Dashboards for Early-Stage Health Innovation

author.name: Svitlana Surodina, Sinem G\"or\"uc\"u, Lili Golmohammadi, Emelia Delaney, Rita Borgo

entry.summary: Designs responsible AI dashboards for early-stage health innovation teams, addressing the gap between abstract responsible AI principles and operational realities of resource-constrained HealthTech development.

entry.title: Modelling and Simulation of Neuromorphic Datasets for Anomaly Detection in Computer Vision

author.name: Mike Middleton, Teymoor Ali, Hakan Kayan, Basabdatta Sen Bhattacharya, Charith Perera, Oliver Rhodes, Elena Gheorghiu, Mark Vousden, Martin A. Trefzer

entry.summary: Introduces ANTShapes, a simulator built in Unity for generating neuromorphic vision datasets with configurable anomaly behaviors. Addresses the scarcity of Dynamic Vision Sensor datasets for anomaly detection research.

entry.title: All Mutation Rates $c/n$ for the $(1+1)$ Evolutionary Algorithm

author.name: Andrew James Kelley

entry.summary: Proves that for every mutation rate c/n with c ≥ 1, there exists a fitness function where this rate is optimal for the (1+1) evolutionary algorithm, showing the set of optimal mutation rates is dense in [1,∞).

entry.title: Tilt-X: Enabling Compliant Aerial Manipulation through a Tiltable-Extensible Continuum Manipulator

author.name: Anuraj Uthayasooriyan, Krishna Manaswi Digumarti, Jack Breward, Fernando Vanegas, Julian Galvez-Serna, Felipe Gonzalez

entry.summary: Presents Tilt-X, a continuum arm aerial manipulator with tilting mechanism, telescopic stage, and cable-driven section that enables volumetric workspace for UAV manipulation beyond just below-vehicle operation.

entry.title: Incremental dimension reduction for efficient and accurate visual anomaly detection

author.name: Teng-Yok Lee

entry.summary: Presents an incremental SVD-based dimension reduction algorithm for visual anomaly detection that processes feature vectors in batches, enabling application to large datasets with thousands of images.

entry.title: Normalisation and Initialisation Strategies for Graph Neural Networks in Blockchain Anomaly Detection

author.name: Dang Sy Duy and Nguyen Duy Chien and Kapil Dev and Jeff Nijsse

entry.summary: Systematic ablation study of initialization and normalization strategies for GNNs on the Elliptic Bitcoin dataset for anti-money laundering, finding these choices are architecture-dependent.

entry.title: Active Learning for Planet Habitability Classification under Extreme Class Imbalance

author.name: R. I. El-Kholy and Z. M. Hayman

entry.summary: Explores active learning for exoplanet habitability classification under extreme class imbalance, combining gradient-boosted trees with pool-based active learning optimized for recall of rare habitable planets.

entry.title: Vision-Language Semantic Grounding for Multi-Domain Crop-Weed Segmentation

author.name: Nazia Hossain, Xintong Jiang, Yu Tian, Philippe Seguin, O. Grant Clark, Shangpeng Sun

entry.summary: Proposes VL-WS, a vision-language framework for crop-weed segmentation that uses frozen CLIP embeddings with FiLM conditioning on natural language captions to achieve domain-invariant representations across heterogeneous agricultural environments.

entry.title: Structured Prompt Optimization for Few-Shot Text Classification via Semantic Alignment in Latent Space

author.name: Jiasen Zheng, Zijun Zhou, Huajun Zhang, Junjiang Lin, Jingyun Jia, Qi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a structured prompt optimization framework for few-shot text classification using multi-dimensional semantic factors with learnable combination mechanisms and contrastive alignment in latent space.

entry.title: MI$^2$DAS: A Multi-Layer Intrusion Detection Framework with Incremental Learning for Securing Industrial IoT Networks

author.name: Wei Lian, Alejandro Guerra-Manzanares

entry.summary: MI²DAS proposes a multi-layer intrusion detection framework for Industrial IoT combining anomaly-based hierarchical traffic pooling, open-set recognition for unknown attacks, and incremental learning for adapting to novel attack types.

entry.title: ULW-SleepNet: An Ultra-Lightweight Network for Multimodal Sleep Stage Scoring

author.name: Zhaowen Wang, Dongdong Zhou, Qi Xu, Fengyu Cong, Mohammad Al-Sa'd, Jenni Raitoharju

entry.summary: ULW-SleepNet is an ultra-lightweight multimodal sleep staging framework using novel Dual-Stream Separable Convolution, parameter sharing, and efficient integration of multiple physiological signals for polysomnography.

entry.title: Exploring Robust Intrusion Detection: A Benchmark Study of Feature Transferability in IoT Botnet Attack Detection

author.name: Alejandro Guerra-Manzanares, Jialin Huang

entry.summary: Benchmarks transferability of three flow-based feature sets across four IoT/IIoT intrusion detection datasets. Finds significant cross-domain performance degradation and identifies features that transfer better using SHAP analysis.

entry.title: GDA-YOLO11: Amodal Instance Segmentation for Occlusion-Robust Robotic Fruit Harvesting

author.name: Caner Beldek, Emre Sariyildiz, Son Lam Phung, and Gursel Alici

entry.summary: Proposes GDA-YOLO11 for amodal instance segmentation in robotic fruit harvesting, predicting full fruit masks including occluded regions. Demonstrates a complete harvesting pipeline from detection to 3D picking point estimation.

entry.title: The GRADIEND Python Package: An End-to-End System for Gradient-Based Feature Learning

author.name: Jonathan Drechsel and Steffen Herbold

entry.summary: Presents gradiend, an open-source Python package implementing the GRADIEND method for learning feature directions from factual-counterfactual gradients in language models, with tools for rewriting and visualization.

entry.title: Bi-level RL-Heuristic Optimization for Real-world Winter Road Maintenance

author.name: Yue Xie, Zizhen Xu, William Beazley, Fumiya Iida

entry.summary: Presents a bi-level optimization framework for winter road maintenance routing, combining RL at the upper level for network partitioning and resource allocation with heuristic-based vehicle routing at the lower level. Validated on real UK road network data.

entry.title: Manifold-Preserving Superpixel Hierarchies and Embeddings for the Exploration of High-Dimensional Images

author.name: Alexander Vieth, Boudewijn Lelieveldt, Elmar Eisemann, Anna Vilanova, Thomas H\"ollt

entry.summary: Introduces a hierarchical embedding technique for high-dimensional images that preserves spatial layout of pixels when constructing hierarchical dimensionality reduction, improving coordinated exploration of image and attribute spaces.

entry.title: ArgLLM-App: An Interactive System for Argumentative Reasoning with Large Language Models

author.name: Adam Dejl, Deniz Gorur, Francesca Toni

entry.summary: Presents ArgLLM-App, a web-based system implementing argumentative LLM agents for binary decision-making tasks, supporting visualization of explanations and human contestation of the system's reasoning.

entry.title: BLISSNet: Deep Operator Learning for Fast and Accurate Flow Reconstruction from Sparse Sensor Measurements

author.name: Maksym Veremchuk, K. Andrea Scott, Zhao Pan

entry.summary: Introduces BLISSNet for reconstructing fluid flows from sparse sensor measurements using a DeepONet-like architecture, balancing accuracy and computational efficiency for both flow reconstruction and data assimilation.

entry.title: Person Identification from Egocentric Human-Object Interactions using 3D Hand Pose

author.name: Muhammad Hamza, Danish Hamid, and Muhammad Tahir Akram

entry.summary: Introduces I2S, a multi-stage framework for user identification through human-object interaction recognition using 3D hand poses from egocentric videos. Targets applications in AR-based personalized assistive technologies.

entry.title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Fast and Data-Efficient Spectrum Allocation in Dynamic Wireless Networks

author.name: Oluwaseyi Giwa and Tobi Awodunmila and Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin and Ahsan Bilal and Muhammad Ali Jamshed

entry.summary: Proposes meta-RL architectures (MAML, RNN, attention-enhanced RNN) for fast adaptation in dynamic 5G/6G spectrum allocation. Shows meta-learning enables sample-efficient learning compared to standard PPO baselines.

entry.title: Task-Lens: Cross-Task Utility Based Speech Dataset Profiling for Low-Resource Indian Languages

author.name: Swati Sharma, Divya V. Sharma, Anubha Gupta

entry.summary: Proposes Task-Lens, a cross-task survey profiling 50 Indian speech datasets across multiple downstream tasks rather than single-task cataloging. Assesses dataset readiness for ASR, TTS, speaker recognition and other tasks.

entry.title: MicroPush: A Simulator and Benchmark for Contact-Rich Cell Pushing and Assembly with a Magnetic Rolling Microrobot

author.name: Yanda Yang and Sambeeta Das

entry.summary: Presents MicroPush, an open-source simulator and benchmark for magnetic rolling microrobots performing cell pushing and assembly in microfluidic environments, with contact-aware physics models.

entry.title: Physics-Embedded Neural ODEs for Learning Antagonistic Pneumatic Artificial Muscle Dynamics

author.name: Xinyao Wang and Jonathan Realmuto

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid Neural ODE framework that embeds physical structure into learned models of antagonistic pneumatic artificial muscle dynamics. Achieves R² of 0.88 across co-contraction conditions by combining parametric joint mechanics with neural network force components.

entry.title: A Boundary Integral-based Neural Operator for Mesh Deformation

author.name: Zhengyu Wu (1), Jun Liu (1), Wei Wang (1) ((1) School of Electronics and Information Engineering.Hangzhou Dianzi University)

entry.summary: Presents a boundary integral-based neural operator (BINO) for mesh deformation, expressing internal displacement solely from boundary data using a Dirichlet-type Green's tensor, avoiding the need to solve for unknown tractions.

entry.title: Altitude-Aware Visual Place Recognition in Top-Down View

author.name: Xingyu Shao, Mengfan He, Chunyu Li, Liangzheng Sun and Ziyang Meng

entry.summary: Proposes an altitude-adaptive aerial visual place recognition method that estimates altitude from ground feature density and uses altitude-based cropping for canonical query images. Achieves robust localization across diverse terrains and altitudes.

entry.title: Autonomous Inspection of Power Line Insulators with UAV on an Unmapped Transmission Tower

author.name: V\'aclav Riss, V\'it Kr\'atk\'y, Robert P\v{e}ni\v{c}ka, Martin Saska

entry.summary: Presents an online UAV inspection algorithm for transmission tower insulators using camera-LiDAR fusion without prior tower maps. Combines CNN detection with DBSCAN/RANSAC/PCA localization.

entry.title: Leveraging Non-linear Dimension Reduction and Random Walk Co-occurrence for Node Embedding

author.name: Ryan DeWolfe

entry.summary: Proposes COVE, an explainable high-dimensional node embedding using random walk co-occurrence and non-linear dimension reduction (UMAP), performing similarly to Louvain for community detection.

entry.title: Agentic AI-RAN: Enabling Intent-Driven, Explainable and Self-Evolving Open RAN Intelligence

author.name: Zhizhou He, Yang Luo, Xinkai Liu, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Mohammad Shojafar, Merouane Debbah, Rahim Tafazolli

entry.summary: Surveys how agentic AI systems with planning, tool use, and memory can be integrated into Open RAN telecommunications architecture for network management, organizing tasks around slice lifecycle, radio resource management, and security/compliance.

entry.title: How IMU Drift Influences Multi-Radar Inertial Odometry for Ground Robots in Subterranean Terrains

author.name: Moumita Mukherjee, Magnus Nor\'en, Anton Koval, Avijit Banerjee, George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage multi-radar inertial odometry framework addressing IMU drift in subterranean environments with smoke, combining an IMU bias estimator with FMCW radar for GPS-denied localization where LiDAR fails.

entry.title: Coverage-Aware Web Crawling for Domain-Specific Supplier Discovery via a Web--Knowledge--Web Pipeline

author.name: Yijiashun Qi, Yijiazhen Qi, Tanmay Wagh

entry.summary: Proposes a Web-Knowledge-Web pipeline for discovering SME suppliers by iteratively crawling web sources, building knowledge graphs, and using graph topology to guide subsequent crawling toward under-discovered supplier regions.

entry.title: An Empirical Review of the Animal Harm Benchmark

author.name: lukasgebhard

entry.summary: Empirically reviews the Animal Harm Benchmark (AHB) for measuring LLM bias against non-human animals, finding that while the benchmark correctly orders risk levels, its effective scoring range is compressed (0.56-0.84), making absolute scores and score differences misleading.

entry.title: Dhati+: Fine-tuned Large Language Models for Arabic Subjectivity Evaluation

author.name: Slimane Bellaouar, Attia Nehar, Soumia Souffi, Mounia Bouameur

entry.summary: Proposes Dhati+, fine-tuned Arabic language models (XLM-RoBERTa, AraBERT, ArabianGPT) for subjectivity evaluation in Arabic text, addressing the scarcity of annotated datasets through a composite dataset AraDhati+.

entry.title: Serendipity with Generative AI: Repurposing knowledge components during polycrisis with a Viable Systems Model approach

author.name: Gordon Fletcher and Saomai Vu Khan

entry.summary: Explores how generative AI can serve as a 'serendipity engine' to discover, classify, and mobilize reusable knowledge components from existing organizational documents. Uses Beer's Viable System Model as an organizing framework.

entry.title: Complex Networks and the Drug Repositioning Problem

author.name: Felipe Bivort Haiek

entry.summary: Studies drug-protein network graph properties for drug repositioning against neglected tropical diseases, using network diffusion for recommendation and identifying crawling vs hopping discovery patterns.

entry.title: Interpretable Multimodal Gesture Recognition for Drone and Mobile Robot Teleoperation via Log-Likelihood Ratio Fusion

author.name: Seungyeol Baek, Jaspreet Singh, Lala Shakti Swarup Ray, Hymalai Bello, Paul Lukowicz, and Sungho Suh

entry.summary: Proposes a multimodal gesture recognition framework for hands-free robot teleoperation, fusing inertial data from Apple Watch with vision via log-likelihood ratio fusion for interpretable decisions in hazardous environments.

entry.title: Denoising-Enhanced YOLO for Robust SAR Ship Detection

author.name: Xiaojing Zhao and Shiyang Li and Zena Chu and Ying Zhang and Peinan Hao and Tianzi Yan and Jiajia Chen and Huicong Ning

entry.summary: CPN-YOLO improves SAR ship detection with a learnable large-kernel denoising module, PPA attention for multi-scale features, and NWD loss function for small target optimization, built on YOLOv8.

entry.title: NAU-QMUL: Utilizing BERT and CLIP for Multi-modal AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Xiaoyu Guo, Arkaitz Zubiaga

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-modal multi-task model using BERT and CLIP for AI-generated image detection and source model identification, achieving 5th place in a competition with pseudo-labeling data augmentation.

entry.title: Teleoperated Omni-directional Dual Arm Mobile Manipulation Robotic System with Shared Control for Retail Store

author.name: Rolif Lima, Somdeb Saha, Nijil George, Vismay Vakharia, Shubham Parab, Sahil Gaonkar, Vighnesh Vatsal and Kaushik Das

entry.summary: Introduces a teleoperated dual-arm mobile robot for retail environments with VR-based shared control and autonomous obstacle avoidance. Demonstrates the system in real retail settings.

entry.title: EDDA-Coordinata: An Annotated Dataset of Historical Geographic Coordinates

author.name: Ludovic Moncla, Pierre Nugues, Thierry Joliveau, Katherine McDonough

entry.summary: Introduces an annotated dataset of historical geographic coordinates from Diderot and d'Alembert's 18th-century Encyclopédie, with trained models for coordinate extraction from historical texts.

entry.title: Learning Robust Control Policies for Inverted Pose on Miniature Blimp Robots

author.name: Yuanlin Yang, Lin Hong, and Fumin Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a simulation-to-real RL framework for controlling miniature blimp robots in inverted poses, using domain randomization and calibrated 3D simulation for robust policy transfer.

entry.title: Unsupervised Baseline Clustering and Incremental Adaptation for IoT Device Traffic Profiling

author.name: Sean M. Alderman, John D. Hastings

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage pipeline for unsupervised IoT traffic profiling using DBSCAN for baseline clustering and BIRCH for incremental adaptation as traffic patterns evolve.

entry.title: Analytical Expression for Spherically Symmetric Photoacoustic Sources: A Unified General Solution (Theoretical Analysis and Derivation)

author.name: Shuang Li, Yibing Wang, Yu Zhang, Changhui Li

entry.summary: Derives analytical expressions for spatiotemporal acoustic pressure from spherically symmetric photoacoustic sources, providing a unified solution for various initial pressure distributions (uniform, Gaussian, exponential, power-law).

entry.title: Blockchain-Enabled Routing for Zero-Trust Low-Altitude Intelligent Networks

author.name: Ziye Jia, Sijie He, Ligang Yuan, Fuhui Zhou, Qihui Wu, Zhu Han, and Dusit Niyato

entry.summary: Proposes a blockchain-enabled zero-trust architecture for secure routing in low-altitude UAV networks, using software-defined perimeter and DRL for optimizing end-to-end routing under security threats. Combines network security with drone networking.

entry.title: Benchmarking BERT-based Models for Sentence-level Topic Classification in Nepali Language

author.name: Nischal Karki, Bipesh Subedi, Prakash Poudyal, Rupak Raj Ghimire, Bal Krishna Bal

entry.summary: Benchmarks various BERT-based models for Nepali sentence-level topic classification, finding that Indic models (MuRIL-large) outperform both multilingual and language-specific models.

entry.title: Micro-expression Recognition Based on Dual-branch Feature Extraction and Fusion

author.name: Mingjie Zhang, Bo Li, Wanting Liu, Hongyan Cui, Yue Li, Qingwen Li, Hong Li, Ge Gao

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-branch micro-expression recognition network with residual and Inception branches plus parallel attention and adaptive fusion. Achieves 74.67% accuracy on CASME II.

entry.title: FaultXformer: A Transformer-Encoder Based Fault Classification and Location Identification model in PMU-Integrated Active Electrical Distribution System

author.name: Kriti Thakur, Alivelu Manga Parimi, Mayukha Pal

entry.summary: Proposes FaultXformer, a Transformer encoder-based architecture for fault detection and localization in electrical distribution systems using PMU current data, handling the complexities introduced by distributed energy resources.

entry.title: Introducing and Deprecating WoFBench

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A humorous meta-commentary on AI benchmarking: presents WoFBench (Wings of Fire knowledge test) and immediately deprecates it because frontier AI models matched superfan-level performance, illustrating how quickly benchmarks become saturated.

entry.title: Uncovering sustainable personal care ingredient combinations using scientific modelling

author.name: Sandip Bhattacharya, Vanessa da Silva, Christina Kohlmann

entry.summary: Uses predictive scientific modeling to discover sustainable natural ingredient combinations for personal care formulations, addressing regulatory pressure to replace synthetic ingredients like silicones. Demonstrates a computational approach to formulation science.

entry.title: Acceleration-Based Control of Fixed-Wing UAVs for Guidance Applications

author.name: Jixiang Wang, Siyuan Yang, Ziyi Wu, Siqi Wei, Ashay Wakode, Agata Barcis, Hung Nguyen and Shaoming He

entry.summary: Presents an acceleration-level outer-loop control framework for fixed-wing UAVs that converts commanded accelerations into body-rate and thrust commands compatible with mainstream autopilots like PX4.

entry.title: Geometry-based pneumatic actuators for soft robotics

author.name: Rui Chen and Daniele Leonardis and Domenico Chiaradia and Antonio Frisoli

entry.summary: Presents geometry-based pneumatic actuators (GPAs) for soft robotics using CNC heat-sealed constraint layers, achieving predictable deformation, near-zero bending radii, and multi-state actuation capabilities.

entry.title: Evaluating Accuracy of Vine Robot Shape Sensing with Distributed Inertial Measurement Units

author.name: Alexis E. Laudenslager, Antonio Alvarez Valdivia, Nathaniel Hanson, and Margaret McGuinness

entry.summary: Evaluates distributed IMU-based shape sensing accuracy for vine robots under active steering, varying robot lengths, and different sensor spacings, building on prior work in soft robot localization.

entry.title: Extended Reality (XR): The Next Frontier in Education

author.name: Shadeeb Hossain

entry.summary: A review article exploring Extended Reality (VR/AR/MR) applications in education, discussing potential benefits, implementation challenges, costs, privacy concerns, and regulatory compliance.

entry.title: A Reliable Indoor Navigation System for Humans Using AR-based Technique

author.name: Vijay U.Rathod, Manav S.Sharma, Shambhavi Verma, Aadi Joshi, Sachin Aage, Sujal Shahane

entry.summary: Implements an AR-based indoor navigation system for campus environments using Vuforia Area Targets for environment modeling and A* algorithm for path calculation, comparing against GPS and Dijkstra approaches.

entry.title: Comparing Classical and Quantum Variational Classifiers on the XOR Problem

author.name: Miras Seilkhan and Adilbek Taizhanov

entry.summary: Compares classical models (logistic regression, MLP) with variational quantum classifiers on the XOR problem, finding performance is determined primarily by model expressivity rather than quantum advantage.

entry.title: Continuously Integrating Feelings: processing feelings moment to moment for reflectively stable policy changes

author.name: Johannes C. Mayer

entry.summary: A lightly edited transcript of a personal introspective conversation with Claude Opus 4.6, exploring how emotions function as heuristic algorithms whose outputs require postprocessing. The author argues that suppressing feelings via superstimuli leads to maladaptive policies, and that integrating emotions leads to more reflectively stable decision-making. Includes a generated song encoding the key ideas.

entry.title: My personal apology to Eliezer Yudkowsky for not working on ASI risk in 2022 itself

author.name: samuelshadrach

entry.summary: A personal reflection and apology for not working on ASI risk starting in 2022, expressing regret about underestimating the pace of AI progress and the difficulty of global coordination. The author notes they are now working full-time on preventing ASI risks and reflects on how three years of delay proved costly.

entry.title: Petapixel cameras won't exist soon

author.name: samuelshadrach

entry.summary: A speculative post about high-resolution surveillance technology and its implications for mutual transparency, arguing that petapixel cameras won't exist soon. The author connects this to broader concerns about ASI governance, advocating for mass movements to counter AI development by the US intelligence community.

entry.title: Research Summary: March 01, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
An unusually thin day for research output. The sole standout is Andrew Critch's (BERI/CHAI) conceptual framework of Schelling goodness — proposing shared morality as a coordination equilibrium among diverse intelligent agents, including AI systems, with direct relevance to multi-agent alignment.

  • A conceptual model frames LLM behavior as navigation through semantic topology with attractor basins, offering intuition for prompt engineering and failure modes
  • The "AI slop as vegan hamburger" analogy provides a useful model for why AI-generated content fails despite surface-level pattern-matching to human output
  • Remaining items cover epistemics, rhetorical analysis, and non-AI topics (lithium/Alzheimer's, meditation) with minimal research substance

Overall, today's pool lacks empirical papers, benchmarks, or technical contributions; only the top three items offer frameworks with any bearing on AI research or practice.

entry.title: Schelling Goodness, and Shared Morality as a Goal

author.name: Andrew_Critch

entry.summary: Andrew Critch introduces 'Schelling goodness' — a framework for thinking about moral coordination among diverse intelligent agents who share no history, where agents try to converge on moral verdicts using only common knowledge and civilizational survival pressures. This connects game theory, moral philosophy, and multi-agent coordination.

entry.title: The Topology of LLM Behavior

author.name: Quentin FEUILLADE--MONTIXI

entry.summary: Presents an intuitive mental model for understanding LLM behavior as navigation through a semantic space with attractors (helpful responses, language matching) and repellers (refusals, safety boundaries), using topological metaphors to explain prompt engineering phenomena like jailbreaks and mode-switching.

entry.title: AI slop is a vegan hamburger

author.name: pku

entry.summary: Uses the analogy of vegan meat substitutes to argue that AI-generated content ('slop') pattern-matches to real content on superficial inspection but fails on deeper engagement, potentially relating this to Kolmogorov complexity differences between genuine and generated content.

entry.title: "Fibbers’ forecasts are worthless"

author.name: Random Developer

entry.summary: Argues that when evaluating practical proposals (not abstract arguments), the credibility and track record of the proposer matters significantly. Draws on Dan Davies' 'One Minute MBA' framework to suggest that known fibbers' forecasts and proposals should be heavily discounted, even in communities that prize idea-over-identity evaluation.

entry.title: Linkpost: "Lithium Prevents Alzheimer’s—Here’s How to Use It"

author.name: Jackson Wagner

entry.summary: Linkpost summarizing evidence that very low-dose lithium supplementation (hundreds to thousands of times below psychiatric doses) may reduce Alzheimer's risk by 20-50%, supported by converging evidence from mouse models, observational studies, psychiatric patient data, and mechanistic research.

entry.title: Burying a Changeling into Foundation of Tower of Knowledge

author.name: siarshai

entry.summary: Describes a rhetorical manipulation technique where a speaker substitutes a secondary aspect of a concept for the whole, builds layers of theory on the altered definition ('buffer overflow'), then uses the conclusions to steer audiences while retaining the emotional weight of the original concept.

entry.title: Mindscapes and Mind Palaces

author.name: Moon Lesbian

entry.summary: Explores the concept of 'mindscapes' — how people visualize the organization of ideas, memories, and emotions in their minds — through informal surveys. Finds most people's mindscapes are disorganized, physical, and primarily visual, and raises concerns about compartmentalization.

entry.title: Jhana 0
entry.summary: Personal reflection on spending a year practicing jhana meditation without achieving any of the eight jhana states. Discusses the technique, the challenges of generating positive feelings as prerequisites, and reflections on the practice.

entry.title: How can rationalists perform exceptionally well?

author.name: pantalaimon

entry.summary: A very brief question post asking what mental tools rationalists could use to perform exceptionally well at novel tasks, using beating a difficult video game on a first try as an example.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 28, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's most impactful work spans AI safety research and a landmark governance crisis between frontier labs and the U.S. military.

  • Model Incrimination (MATS 9.0 / Neel Nanda) introduces novel methods to diagnose *why* an LLM misbehaves—distinguishing scheming from sycophancy or capability failures—filling a critical gap in safety evaluation
  • Unsupervised Elicitation research (MATS/Anthropic) delivers an important negative result: no existing easy-to-hard generalization technique reliably scales oversight to superhuman models across three realistic challenge settings
  • The Dawn of AI Scheming provides the most comprehensive survey to date of empirical evidence on deceptive alignment across model organisms

On governance, Zvi's analysis of the Anthropic–Department of War standoff and Sam Altman's memo aligning OpenAI with Anthropic's red lines on autonomous weapons and mass surveillance represent a potential inflection point for military AI policy. New ARENA exercise sets package frontier interpretability topics (attribution graphs, emergent features) into accessible training material. Abram Demski's Coherent Care advances foundational arguments for Updateless Decision Theory, and a community-built RSP version comparison tool aids timely policy scrutiny.

entry.title: Anthropic and the DoW: Anthropic Responds

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from Research two days ago on the Anthropic-DoW confrontation, Zvi analyzes the escalating confrontation between the Department of War and Anthropic, where the Pentagon demanded 'unfettered access' to Claude for all lawful military uses or face designation as a supply chain risk or invocation of the Defense Production Act. The piece covers Anthropic's response, broader industry reactions, and the legal and governance implications of government coercion of AI companies.

entry.title: Sam Altman says OpenAI shares Anthropic's red lines in Pentagon fight

author.name: Matrice Jacobine

entry.summary: Building on yesterday's News coverage of Anthropic's refusal, Sam Altman circulated an internal memo stating OpenAI will draw the same red lines as Anthropic regarding Pentagon AI use—no mass surveillance or autonomous lethal weapons. This represents a potential industry-wide unified stance that could complicate the Pentagon's efforts to replace Anthropic with another AI provider.

entry.title: Why Did My Model Do That? Model Incrimination for Diagnosing LLM Misbehavior

author.name: aditya singh

entry.summary: MATS 9.0 research (advised by Neel Nanda) introducing 'model incrimination'—methods to determine whether a model's suspicious behavior stems from scheming, confusion, or mistakes. They build environments where models take concerning actions and use interpretability techniques to investigate the underlying motivations, aiming to help labs distinguish genuine scheming from benign errors.

entry.title: 3 Challenges and 2 Hopes for the Safety of Unsupervised Elicitation

author.name: Callum Canavan

entry.summary: Research from MATS/Anthropic fellowship studying three realistic challenges to unsupervised elicitation and easy-to-hard generalization techniques for steering models on superhuman tasks. They stress-test existing techniques and two new approaches (ensembling, combined methods), finding that no technique reliably overcomes all three challenges.

entry.title: New ARENA material: 8 exercise sets on alignment science & interpretability

author.name: CallumMcDougall

entry.summary: Callum McDougall announces 8 new ARENA exercise sets covering cutting-edge alignment and interpretability topics including attribution graphs, emergent misalignment, alignment faking, reasoning model interpretability (Thought Anchors), and persona vectors. Each set contains 1-2 days of hands-on material for upskilling researchers.

entry.title: The Dawn of AI Scheming

author.name: Alvin Ånestrand

entry.summary: A comprehensive aggregation of virtually everything currently known about AI scheming (deceptive alignment), covering empirical evidence from model organisms, theoretical arguments, and building toward an informed forecast. Written primarily during autumn 2025, it serves as a reference document for the scheming threat model.

entry.title: Side by Side Comparison of RSP Versions

author.name: Corm

entry.summary: Following News coverage from two days ago of Anthropic's RSP changes, A community member created a side-by-side comparison website for all versions of Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP), making it easy to track how the policy has evolved. The author notes a clear shift from firm commitments to softer reporting language across versions.

entry.title: Coherent Care

author.name: abramdemski

entry.summary: Abram Demski presents careful arguments for Updateless Decision Theory (UDT) over naively updateful theories like CDT and EDT, framed through his ongoing tiling theorem research agenda. The essay develops the idea that rational agents should 'care coherently' about outcomes in a way that motivates updateless reasoning, with implications for AI safety foundations.

entry.title: Safe ASI Is Achievable: The Finite Game Argument

author.name: Lester Leong

entry.summary: An essay arguing that safe ASI is achievable by framing alignment as a 'finite game' with identifiable win conditions, written against the backdrop of Anthropic's RSP changes and rapidly advancing model capabilities (Opus 4.6, Codex 5.3). The author attempts to provide an optimistic but grounded framework for why alignment challenges are solvable.

entry.title: Vibe Coding is a System Design Interview

author.name: Brendan Long

entry.summary: A practitioner's observation that effective 'vibe coding' (AI-assisted programming) converges on skills similar to system design interviews: writing detailed specifications, thinking through edge cases, and making architectural tradeoffs, rather than writing code directly.

entry.title: Ball+Gravity has a "Downhill" Preference

author.name: TristanTrim

entry.summary: A thought experiment exploring how physical systems like a ball rolling downhill can be described using the language of preferences from Optimal Information Structure (OIS) theory. The author argues that composite systems (ball+gravity) exhibit preferences in a technical sense analogous to human preferences.

entry.title: AI Security Bootcamp Singapore - Call for Applications

author.name: Pranav Gade

entry.summary: Announcement for a 7-day intensive AI security bootcamp in Singapore targeting experienced security professionals, covering threat modeling for frontier AI systems, adversarial misuse, loss-of-control risks, and governance interventions. This is the second iteration after a London program in August 2025.

entry.title: Best short introductions to AI safety & alignment for bright college students?

author.name: geoffreymiller

entry.summary: Geoffrey Miller asks the LessWrong community to recommend short, accessible introductions to AI safety and alignment suitable for Oxford PPE undergraduates who may go on to influential positions in government and industry.

entry.title: What I Got From 1.5 Years In Slightly-Competitive Debate

author.name: CarolusRenniusVitellius

entry.summary: A personal reflection on how 1.5 years of British Parliamentary debate at TU Delft improved the author's rationality, open-mindedness, and scientific thinking, contrary to the common assumption that competitive debate undermines truth-seeking.

entry.title: The tick in my back

author.name: benjamin ar

entry.summary: A personal essay using the metaphor of a tick to describe the author's experience with what appears to be a chronic condition acquired in childhood in Maine. The piece reflects on shifts from curiosity-driven Montessori learning to more constrained educational environments.

entry.title: Here's to the Polypropylene Makers

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A tribute to the roughly 80 workers at Braskem America's polypropylene plants who voluntarily quarantined inside their factories for weeks during early COVID-19 to ensure continued production of the raw material needed for N95 masks.

entry.title: Research Summary: February 27, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
AI safety and biosecurity research dominate today's highlights. A rigorous human uplift study shows LLM access yields a 4.16x accuracy boost for novices on dual-use biology tasks, with major policy implications. AuditBench provides 56 models with implanted hidden behaviors for evaluating alignment auditing, while a novel 'self-incrimination training' approach teaches GPT-4.1 and Gemini-2.0 agents to report their own deceptive behavior. A blog post argues eval awareness may emerge as a training artifact rather than a pure capability.

  • Semantic Tube Prediction, a JEPA-style method co-authored by Yann LeCun, claims to beat LLM data efficiency via the Geodesic Hypothesis on semantic manifolds
  • ArchAgent, built on AlphaEvolve, autonomously discovers cache replacement policies matching expert-designed heuristics in two days
  • Independently trained transformers converge to the same algorithmic cores—compact invariant subspaces necessary and sufficient for task performance
  • RKSP predicts training divergence from a single forward pass at initialization with 0.995 AUROC
  • A decision-theoretic steganography framework from Krueger, Tegmark, and van der Schaar formalizes detection limits for covert LLM communication
  • LeRobot from HuggingFace delivers an end-to-end open-source robot learning stack spanning teleoperation to large-scale policy training

entry.title: Scoop: Pentagon takes first step toward blacklisting Anthropic

author.name: Matrice Jacobine

entry.summary: Reports the Pentagon asked Boeing and Lockheed Martin to assess their reliance on Anthropic's Claude, a first step toward designating Anthropic as a 'supply chain risk' - a penalty usually reserved for adversarial nations.

entry.title: Anthropic: "Statement from Dario Amodei on our discussions with the Department of War"

author.name: Matrice Jacobine

entry.summary: Reposts Dario Amodei's statement on Anthropic's work with the Department of War, emphasizing their commitment to deploying AI for US defense and democracy while maintaining red lines on domestic surveillance and autonomous killing.

entry.title: LLM Novice Uplift on Dual-Use, In Silico Biology Tasks

author.name: Chen Bo Calvin Zhang, Christina Q. Knight, Nicholas Kruus, Jason Hausenloy, Pedro Medeiros, Nathaniel Li, Aiden Kim, Yury Orlovskiy, Coleman Breen, Bryce Cai, Jasper G\"otting, Andrew Bo Liu, Samira Nedungadi, Paula Rodriguez, Yannis Yiming He, Mohamed Shaaban, Zifan Wang, Seth Donoughe, Julian Michael

entry.summary: Conducts a multi-model human uplift study showing LLM access makes novices 4.16x more accurate on biosecurity-relevant biology tasks compared to internet-only access. On some benchmarks, novices with LLMs matched or exceeded domain experts.

entry.title: ArchAgent: Agentic AI-driven Computer Architecture Discovery

author.name: Raghav Gupta, Akanksha Jain, Abraham Gonzalez, Alexander Novikov, Po-Sen Huang, Matej Balog, Marvin Eisenberger, Sergey Shirobokov, Ng\^an V\~u, Martin Dixon, Borivoje Nikoli\'c, Parthasarathy Ranganathan, Sagar Karandikar

entry.summary: Presents ArchAgent, built on AlphaEvolve, that automatically discovers computer architecture designs—specifically cache replacement policies. In two days without human intervention, it generated policies competitive with state-of-the-art within an established design competition framework.

entry.title: Training Agents to Self-Report Misbehavior

author.name: Bruce W. Lee, Chen Yueh-Han, Tomek Korbak

entry.summary: As covered in Research yesterday, Proposes 'self-incrimination training' that trains AI agents (GPT-4.1 and Gemini-2.0) to call a report_scheming() tool when behaving deceptively. Significantly reduces undetected attack rates while preserving instruction hierarchy, outperforming monitors and alignment baselines.

entry.title: Semantic Tube Prediction: Beating LLM Data Efficiency with JEPA

author.name: Hai Huang, Yann LeCun, Randall Balestriero

entry.summary: Introduces Semantic Tube Prediction, a JEPA-style regularizer based on the Geodesic Hypothesis that token sequences trace geodesics on a semantic manifold, improving LLM data efficiency by 2-3x and challenging standard scaling laws.

entry.title: AuditBench: Evaluating Alignment Auditing Techniques on Models with Hidden Behaviors

author.name: Abhay Sheshadri, Aidan Ewart, Kai Fronsdal, Isha Gupta, Samuel R. Bowman, Sara Price, Samuel Marks, Rowan Wang

entry.summary: AuditBench introduces a benchmark of 56 language models with implanted hidden behaviors (sycophancy, opposition to AI regulation, secret loyalties) that models don't confess when directly asked, used to evaluate alignment auditing techniques with an investigator agent.

entry.title: How eval awareness might emerge in training

author.name: Igor Ivanov

entry.summary: Explores how evaluation awareness might emerge during model training rather than being purely a capability scaling phenomenon. Notes Apollo Research found Claude Opus 4.6 had high eval awareness that undermined safety testing.

entry.title: Why Diffusion Language Models Struggle with Truly Parallel (Non-Autoregressive) Decoding?

author.name: Pengxiang Li, Dilxat Muhtar, Lu Yin, Tianlong Chen, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: Analyzes why diffusion language models converge to autoregressive-like decoding despite being designed for parallel generation, attributing this to a mismatch between DLM objectives and sequential training data structure. Proposes NAP for truly non-autoregressive generation.

entry.title: A Decision-Theoretic Formalisation of Steganography With Applications to LLM Monitoring

author.name: Usman Anwar, Julianna Piskorz, David D. Baek, David Africa, Jim Weatherall, Max Tegmark, Christian Schroeder de Witt, Mihaela van der Schaar, David Krueger

entry.summary: Proposes a decision-theoretic framework for detecting steganography in LLM outputs, addressing the challenge that classical steganography detection requires a known reference distribution. Central insight: steganography creates information asymmetry between decoders and non-decoders.

entry.title: Residual Koopman Spectral Profiling for Predicting and Preventing Transformer Training Instability

author.name: Bum Jun Kim, Shohei Taniguchi, Makoto Kawano, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: RKSP uses Koopman spectral analysis on a single forward pass at initialization to predict transformer training divergence with 0.995 AUROC, providing failure probability estimates before expensive training runs begin.

entry.title: Modality Collapse as Mismatched Decoding: Information-Theoretic Limits of Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Jayadev Billa

entry.summary: This paper formalizes 'modality collapse' in multimodal LLMs as a mismatched decoder problem, showing that modality-specific information (speaker identity, emotion) survives through LLM layers but the text-trained decoder cannot use it. Bounded by Generalized Mutual Information.

entry.title: LeRobot: An Open-Source Library for End-to-End Robot Learning

author.name: Remi Cadene, Simon Aliberts, Francesco Capuano, Michel Aractingi, Adil Zouitine, Pepijn Kooijmans, Jade Choghari, Martino Russi, Caroline Pascal, Steven Palma, Mustafa Shukor, Jess Moss, Alexander Soare, Dana Aubakirova, Quentin Lhoest, Quentin Gallou\'edec, Thomas Wolf

entry.summary: Presents LeRobot, an open-source library integrating the entire robot learning stack from motor control to large-scale learning methods. Covers teleoperation, datasets, and scalable learning pipelines.

entry.title: Transformers converge to invariant algorithmic cores

author.name: Joshua S. Schiffman

entry.summary: Demonstrates that independently trained transformers converge to the same 'algorithmic cores' - compact subspaces necessary and sufficient for task performance. Shows Markov-chain transformers embed 3D cores in orthogonal subspaces but recover identical transition spectra.

entry.title: IMMACULATE: A Practical LLM Auditing Framework via Verifiable Computation

author.name: Yanpei Guo, Wenjie Qu, Linyu Wu, Shengfang Zhai, Lionel Z. Wang, Ming Xu, Yue Liu, Binhang Yuan, Dawn Song, Jiaheng Zhang

entry.summary: IMMACULATE is a practical auditing framework that detects LLM provider deviations like model substitution, quantization abuse, and token overbilling using verifiable computation on a small fraction of requests. It achieves strong detection with under 1% throughput overhead.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling with Diffusion Language Models via Reward-Guided Stitching

author.name: Roy Miles, Aysim Toker, Andreea-Maria Oncescu, Songcen Xu, Jiankang Deng, Ismail Elezi

entry.summary: Proposes reward-guided stitching for test-time scaling with diffusion language models: sampling diverse reasoning trajectories, scoring intermediate steps with a process reward model, and stitching best steps across trajectories into coherent solutions.

entry.title: CLIP Is Shortsighted: Paying Attention Beyond the First Sentence

author.name: Marc-Antoine Lavoie, Anas Mahmoud, Aldo Zaimi, Arsene Fansi Tchango, Steven L. Waslander

entry.summary: Reveals that CLIP models are biased toward encoding only the first sentence of long captions due to training data structure where both human and LLM captions begin with summaries. Proposes methods to mitigate this 'shortsightedness' for better long-caption understanding.

entry.title: TrajTok: Learning Trajectory Tokens enables better Video Understanding

author.name: Chenhao Zheng, Jieyu Zhang, Jianing Zhang, Weikai Huang, Ashutosh Kumar, Quan Kong, Oncel Tuzel, Chun-Liang Li, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Proposes TrajTok, an end-to-end video tokenizer that performs implicit spatio-temporal clustering to produce trajectory-based tokens co-trained with video models, decoupling token count from video duration while adapting granularity to semantic complexity.

entry.title: Certified Circuits: Stability Guarantees for Mechanistic Circuits

author.name: Alaa Anani, Tobias Lorenz, Bernt Schiele, Mario Fritz, Jonas Fischer

entry.summary: Introduces Certified Circuits, providing provable stability guarantees for mechanistic circuit discovery in neural networks. Uses randomized data subsampling to certify that circuit component decisions are invariant to bounded dataset changes.

entry.title: Zatom-1: A Multimodal Flow Foundation Model for 3D Molecules and Materials

author.name: Alex Morehead, Miruna Cretu, Antonia Panescu, Rishabh Anand, Maurice Weiler, Tynan Perez, Samuel Blau, Steven Farrell, Wahid Bhimji, Anubhav Jain, Hrushikesh Sahasrabuddhe, Pietro Lio, Tommi Jaakkola, Rafael Gomez-Bombarelli, Rex Ying, N. Benjamin Erichson, Michael W. Mahoney

entry.summary: Introduces Zatom-1, the first foundation model unifying generative and predictive learning for both 3D molecules and materials using multimodal flow matching over discrete atom types and continuous geometries. Shows scalable pretraining with predictable gains.

entry.title: ContextRL: Enhancing MLLM's Knowledge Discovery Efficiency with Context-Augmented RL

author.name: Xingyu Lu, Jinpeng Wang, YiFan Zhang, Shijie Ma, Xiao Hu, Tianke Zhang, Haonan fan, Kaiyu Jiang, Changyi Liu, Kaiyu Tang, Bin Wen, Fan Yang, Tingting Gao, Han Li, Chun Yuan

entry.summary: ContextRL improves reinforcement learning for multimodal LLMs by providing reward models with full reference solutions as context to filter false positives, and using multi-turn sampling with mistake reports to recover from failed attempts. Results show significant improvements across 11 perception and reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Unleashing the Potential of Diffusion Models for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yinan Zheng, Tianyi Tan, Bin Huang, Enguang Liu, Ruiming Liang, Jianlin Zhang, Jianwei Cui, Guang Chen, Kun Ma, Hangjun Ye, Long Chen, Ya-Qin Zhang, Xianyuan Zhan, Jingjing Liu

entry.summary: This paper presents a large-scale investigation of diffusion models as planners for end-to-end autonomous driving, using real-vehicle data and road testing rather than simulation-only evaluation. Key insights are identified through controlled studies.

entry.title: NoRA: Breaking the Linear Ceiling of Low-Rank Adaptation via Manifold Expansion

author.name: Hung-Hsuan Chen

entry.summary: NoRA introduces non-linear rank adaptation with SiLU gating and structural dropout for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, breaking LoRA's 'linear ceiling' where increasing rank yields diminishing returns. NoRA at rank 64 outperforms LoRA at rank 512.

entry.title: Support Tokens, Stability Margins, and a New Foundation for Robust LLMs

author.name: Deepak Agarwal, Dhyey Dharmendrakumar Mavani, Suyash Gupta, Karthik Sethuraman, Tejas Dharamsi

entry.summary: Reinterprets causal self-attention in transformers through a probabilistic framework, revealing a barrier constraint on attention parameters that induces structured geometry on token space. Draws analogies to support vectors and stability margins from classical ML.

entry.title: Causality $\neq$ Invariance: Function and Concept Vectors in LLMs

author.name: Gustaw Opie{\l}ka, Hannes Rosenbusch, Claire E. Stevenson

entry.summary: Reveals that Function Vectors in LLMs, which causally drive in-context learning, are not format-invariant—they become nearly orthogonal when extracted from different input formats. Introduces Concept Vectors (CVs) that carry more stable concept representations using Representational Similarity Analysis.

entry.title: Flow Matching is Adaptive to Manifold Structures

author.name: Shivam Kumar, Yixin Wang, Lizhen Lin

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical analysis showing flow matching is adaptive to low-dimensional manifold structure in data, explaining its empirical success in high-dimensional settings like image and video generation where data lies on low-dimensional manifolds.

entry.title: Imagination Helps Visual Reasoning, But Not Yet in Latent Space

author.name: You Li, Chi Chen, Yanghao Li, Fanhu Zeng, Kaiyu Huang, Jinan Xu, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Using Causal Mediation Analysis, reveals that latent visual reasoning in MLLMs has critical disconnections: input perturbations barely affect latent tokens, and latent token perturbations barely affect outputs, suggesting latent reasoning doesn't work as intended.

entry.title: Vision Transformers Need More Than Registers

author.name: Cheng Shi, Yizhou Yu, Sibei Yang

entry.summary: Identifies that Vision Transformer artifacts stem from 'lazy aggregation' where ViTs use background patches as shortcuts for global semantics. Proposes selective integration of patch features into CLS token to reduce artifacts beyond what register tokens alone achieve.

entry.title: HulluEdit: Single-Pass Evidence-Consistent Subspace Editing for Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yangguang Lin, Quan Fang, Yufei Li, Jiachen Sun, Junyu Gao, Jitao Sang

entry.summary: Introduces HulluEdit, a single-pass reference-free framework for mitigating hallucinations in large vision-language models through orthogonal subspace editing that decomposes hidden states into visual evidence, conflicting priors, and residual uncertainty.

entry.title: Inference-time Generative Debates on Coding and Reasoning Tasks for Scalable Oversight

author.name: ethanelasky

entry.summary: Tests generative debate for scalable oversight on coding and reasoning tasks. Finds mostly negative results: debate underperforms consultancy in 11/16 conditions, and removing transcripts matches or outperforms both methods.

entry.title: Mirroring the Mind: Distilling Human-Like Metacognitive Strategies into Large Language Models

author.name: Ik-hwan Kim, Hyeongrok Han, Mingi Jung, Sangwon Yu, Jinseok Hong, Sang Hun Kim, Yoonyoung Choi, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes Metacognitive Behavioral Tuning (MBT), a post-training framework that injects metacognitive behaviors into reasoning models to address structural fragility—where models fail despite valid intermediate steps due to lack of self-regulatory control.

entry.title: veScale-FSDP: Flexible and High-Performance FSDP at Scale

author.name: Zezhou Wang, Youjie Li, Zhiqi Lin, Jiacheng Yang, Cong Xie, Guanyu Feng, Zheng Zhong, Ziyue Huang, Hongyu Zhu, Zhi Zhang, Yanghua Peng, Xin Liu

entry.summary: Introduces veScale-FSDP with RaggedShard flexible sharding format, supporting structure-aware training methods (block-wise quantization) and non-element-wise optimizers (Shampoo, Muon) used in Gemini and Kimi K2. Achieves 2-6x communication reduction.

entry.title: Silent Egress: When Implicit Prompt Injection Makes LLM Agents Leak Without a Trace

author.name: Qianlong Lan, Anuj Kaul, Shaun Jones, Stephanie Westrum

entry.summary: Demonstrates 'silent egress' attacks where implicit prompt injection via URL previews causes LLM agents to exfiltrate sensitive runtime context. Achieves 89% success rate with a qwen2.5:7b agent, with 95% of successful attacks appearing benign to users.

entry.title: AgentSentry: Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Temporal Causal Diagnostics and Context Purification

author.name: Tian Zhang, Yiwei Xu, Juan Wang, Keyan Guo, Xiaoyang Xu, Bowen Xiao, Quanlong Guan, Jinlin Fan, Jiawei Liu, Zhiquan Liu, Hongxin Hu

entry.summary: AgentSentry defends LLM agents against indirect prompt injection attacks using temporal causal diagnostics to disentangle malicious control from legitimate task execution across multi-turn trajectories, combined with context purification.

entry.title: FlashOptim: Optimizers for Memory Efficient Training

author.name: Jose Javier Gonzalez Ortiz, Abhay Gupta, Chris Renard, Davis Blalock

entry.summary: FlashOptim reduces per-parameter training memory by over 50% through improved master weight splitting with tight quantization error bounds and companding functions, while preserving model quality and API compatibility.

entry.title: Model Agreement via Anchoring

author.name: Eric Eaton, Surbhi Goel, Marcel Hussing, Michael Kearns, Aaron Roth, Sikata Bela Sengupta, Jessica Sorrell

entry.summary: Develops a general technique for bounding model disagreement between independently trained models using 'anchoring' to the average model. Provides theoretical guarantees that disagreement can be driven to zero. Authors include Michael Kearns and Aaron Roth.

entry.title: RAIN-Merging: A Gradient-Free Method to Enhance Instruction Following in Large Reasoning Models with Preserved Thinking Format

author.name: Zhehao Huang, Yuhang Liu, Baijiong Lin, Yixin Lou, Zhengbao He, Hanling Tian, Tao Li, Xiaolin Huang

entry.summary: Proposes RAIN-Merging, a method to improve instruction following in large reasoning models by merging instruction-tuned models while preserving the thinking format, finding that task vectors of LRMs and ITMs occupy nearly orthogonal subspaces.

entry.title: TorchLean: Formalizing Neural Networks in Lean

author.name: Robert Joseph George, Jennifer Cruden, Xiangru Zhong, Huan Zhang, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: TorchLean formalizes neural networks in the Lean 4 theorem prover, treating models as first-class mathematical objects with unified semantics for execution and verification, bridging the gap between deployed models and formally verified properties.

entry.title: Scale Can't Overcome Pragmatics: The Impact of Reporting Bias on Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Amita Kamath, Jack Hessel, Khyathi Chandu, Jena D. Hwang, Kai-Wei Chang, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Demonstrates that reporting bias in VLM training data—where people omit tacit information in captions—leads to insufficient representation of spatial, temporal, negation, and counting reasoning skills, persisting despite web-scale data and/or post-training.

entry.title: A data- and compute-efficient chest X-ray foundation model beyond aggressive scaling

author.name: Chong Wang, Yabin Zhang, Yunhe Gao, Maya Varma, Clemence Mottez, Faidra Patsatzi, Jiaming Liu, Jin Long, Jean-Benoit Delbrouck, Sergios Gatidis, Akshay S. Chaudhari, Curtis P. Langlotz

entry.summary: Introduces CheXficient, a chest X-ray foundation model that uses active data curation during pretraining as an alternative to brute-force dataset scaling, demonstrating that principled data selection can match or exceed larger-scale training. From Stanford group.

entry.title: A Positive Case for Faithfulness: LLM Self-Explanations Help Predict Model Behavior

author.name: harrymayne

entry.summary: Introduces a new faithfulness metric measuring whether LLM self-explanations help humans predict model behavior on related inputs. Finds self-explanations consistently help prediction, providing a positive case for CoT faithfulness.

entry.title: How Do Latent Reasoning Methods Perform Under Weak and Strong Supervision?

author.name: Yingqian Cui, Zhenwei Dai, Bing He, Zhan Shi, Hui Liu, Rui Sun, Zhiji Liu, Yue Xing, Jiliang Tang, Benoit Dumoulin

entry.summary: Conducts comprehensive analysis of latent reasoning methods (reasoning in continuous space rather than text), identifying pervasive shortcut learning under weak supervision and revealing that latent representations under different supervision levels behave differently.

entry.title: CourtGuard: A Model-Agnostic Framework for Zero-Shot Policy Adaptation in LLM Safety

author.name: Umid Suleymanov, Rufiz Bayramov, Suad Gafarli, Seljan Musayeva, Taghi Mammadov, Aynur Akhundlu, Murat Kantarcioglu

entry.summary: Introduces CourtGuard, a retrieval-augmented multi-agent framework that treats safety evaluation as adversarial evidentiary debate. Achieves SOTA across 7 safety benchmarks with zero-shot adaptability to new policies without fine-tuning.

entry.title: A Model-Free Universal AI

author.name: Yegon Kim, Juho Lee

entry.summary: Introduces AIQI, the first model-free agent proven asymptotically ε-optimal in general reinforcement learning, performing universal induction over distributional action-value functions instead of environment models.

entry.title: Multi-Dimensional Spectral Geometry of Biological Knowledge in Single-Cell Transformer Representations

author.name: Ihor Kendiukhov

entry.summary: Systematically decodes the geometric structure of scGPT's internal representations through 183 automated hypotheses, revealing that the model organizes genes into a structured biological coordinate system where the dominant spectral axis separates genes by subcellular localization.

entry.title: Manifold of Failure: Behavioral Attraction Basins in Language Models

author.name: Sarthak Munshi, Manish Bhatt, Vineeth Sai Narajala, Idan Habler, AmmarnAl-Kahfah, Ken Huang, Blake Gatto

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for mapping the 'Manifold of Failure' in LLMs using MAP-Elites quality-diversity search to illuminate behavioral attraction basins where models diverge from alignment. Tests on Llama-3-8B, GPT-OSS-20B, and GPT-5-Mini.

entry.title: Calibrated Test-Time Guidance for Bayesian Inference

author.name: Daniel Geyfman, Felix Draxler, Jan Groeneveld, Hyunsoo Lee, Theofanis Karaletsos, Stephan Mandt

entry.summary: Proposes calibrated test-time guidance methods for diffusion models that correctly sample from the Bayesian posterior rather than just maximizing reward. Shows existing guidance methods fail to recover correct posteriors and provides consistent alternative estimators.

entry.title: Reinforcement-aware Knowledge Distillation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zhaoyang Zhang, Shuli Jiang, Yantao Shen, Yuting Zhang, Dhananjay Ram, Shuo Yang, Zhuowen Tu, Wei Xia, Stefano Soatto

entry.summary: Proposes reinforcement-aware knowledge distillation for LLM reasoning that addresses distribution mismatch and objective interference when combining KD with RL. Integrates distillation directly into the RL process rather than treating them as separate objectives.

entry.title: Distributed LLM Pretraining During Renewable Curtailment Windows: A Feasibility Study

author.name: Philipp Wiesner, Soeren Becker, Brett Cornick, Dominik Scheinert, Alexander Acker, Odej Kao

entry.summary: This paper presents a system for distributed LLM pretraining during renewable energy curtailment windows, elastically switching between single-site and federated multi-site training as sites become available. It demonstrates feasibility of using otherwise-wasted clean energy for training.

entry.title: Probing for Knowledge Attribution in Large Language Models

author.name: Ivo Brink, Alexander Boer, Dennis Ulmer

entry.summary: This work shows that simple linear probes on LLM hidden representations can reliably predict whether a model's output is based on the prompt context or its internal knowledge (contributive attribution). Introduces AttriWiki, a self-supervised data pipeline for training such probes.

entry.title: Exploratory Memory-Augmented LLM Agent via Hybrid On- and Off-Policy Optimization

author.name: Zeyuan Liu, Jeonghye Kim, Xufang Luo, Dongsheng Li, Yuqing Yang

entry.summary: EMPO² combines memory-augmented exploration with hybrid on- and off-policy RL optimization for LLM agents, achieving 128.6% improvement over GRPO on ScienceWorld and showing strong out-of-distribution generalization.

entry.title: Multilingual Safety Alignment Via Sparse Weight Editing

author.name: Jiaming Liang, Zhaoxin Wang, Handing Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free framework for multilingual safety alignment in LLMs via sparse weight editing, identifying safety neurons and mapping their activations across languages through a closed-form linear transformation.

entry.title: Accelerating LLM Pre-Training through Flat-Direction Dynamics Enhancement

author.name: Shuchen Zhu, Rizhen Hu, Mingze Wang, Mou Sun, Xue Wang, Kun Yuan, Zaiwen Wen

entry.summary: Proposes accelerating LLM pre-training by enhancing optimization along flat directions of the loss landscape, presenting a unified Riemannian ODE framework explaining how adaptive optimizers work and introducing FOCUS optimizer.

entry.title: Interpreting and Steering State-Space Models via Activation Subspace Bottlenecks

author.name: Vamshi Sunku Mohan, Kaustubh Gupta, Aneesha Das, Chandan Singh

entry.summary: Identifies activation subspace bottlenecks in Mamba SSM models using mechanistic interpretability tools and introduces a simple test-time steering intervention (scalar multiplication) that improves performance by 8.27% on average across 5 SSMs and 6 benchmarks.

entry.title: SimpleOCR: Rendering Visualized Questions to Teach MLLMs to Read

author.name: Yibo Peng, Peng Xia, Ding Zhong, Kaide Zeng, Siwei Han, Yiyang Zhou, Jiaqi Liu, Ruiyi Zhang, Huaxiu Yao

entry.summary: Diagnoses that multimodal LLMs suffer from 'modality laziness'—up to 12.7% performance drop when text queries are rendered onto images—revealing they rely on text shortcuts rather than genuinely reading image text. Proposes SimpleOCR training approach to bridge this gap.

entry.title: Towards Better RL Training Data Utilization via Second-Order Rollout

author.name: Zhe Yang, Yudong Wang, Rang Li, Zhifang Sui

entry.summary: Proposes second-order rollout for RL training of LLMs, generating multiple critiques for responses (not just multiple responses for questions), enabling joint training of generation and critique capabilities for more effective data utilization.

entry.title: GeoWorld: Geometric World Models

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Danning Li, Ian Reid, Richard Hartley

entry.summary: Introduces GeoWorld, a geometric world model using Hyperbolic JEPA to map latent representations onto hyperbolic manifolds, preserving hierarchical structure for improved long-horizon prediction in visual planning.

entry.title: AgentVista: Evaluating Multimodal Agents in Ultra-Challenging Realistic Visual Scenarios

author.name: Zhaochen Su, Jincheng Gao, Hangyu Guo, Zhenhua Liu, Lueyang Zhang, Xinyu Geng, Shijue Huang, Peng Xia, Guanyu Jiang, Cheng Wang, Yue Zhang, Yi R. Fung, Junxian He

entry.summary: Introduces AgentVista, a benchmark for multimodal agents spanning 25 sub-domains across 7 categories, pairing realistic visual scenarios with natural hybrid tool use requiring multi-step reasoning grounded in visual evidence.

entry.title: Decomposing Private Image Generation via Coarse-to-Fine Wavelet Modeling

author.name: Jasmine Bayrooti, Weiwei Kong, Natalia Ponomareva, Carlos Esteves, Ameesh Makadia, Amanda Prorok

entry.summary: Proposes a spectral differential privacy framework that applies stronger privacy protection to low-frequency image components (which contain privacy-sensitive features) while allowing high-frequency details to train more freely. Achieves better image quality under DP constraints.

entry.title: VGG-T$^3$: Offline Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction at Scale

author.name: Sven Elflein, Ruilong Li, S\'ergio Agostinho, Zan Gojcic, Laura Leal-Taix\'e, Qunjie Zhou, Aljosa Osep

entry.summary: Presents VGG-T³, a scalable 3D reconstruction method that distills scene geometry into fixed-size MLPs via test-time training, achieving linear scaling with input views. Reconstructs 1k images in 54 seconds with 11.6x speedup over attention-based baselines.

entry.title: SideQuest: Model-Driven KV Cache Management for Long-Horizon Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Sanjay Kariyappa, G. Edward Suh

entry.summary: Proposes SideQuest, a KV cache compression approach that uses the reasoning model itself to decide which tokens to keep, preventing context pollution by isolating the cache management reasoning in a separate 'side quest'.

entry.title: Towards Autonomous Memory Agents

author.name: Xinle Wu, Rui Zhang, Mustafa Anis Hussain, Yao Lu

entry.summary: Proposes autonomous memory agents that proactively acquire, validate, and curate knowledge rather than passively storing conversation history. U-Mem uses a cost-aware knowledge extraction cascade and semantic-aware Thompson sampling for active knowledge seeking.

entry.title: Know What You Know: Metacognitive Entropy Calibration for Verifiable RL Reasoning

author.name: Qiannian Zhao, Chen Yang, Jinhao Jing, Yunke Zhang, Xuhui Ren, Lu Yu, Shijie Zhang, Hongzhi Yin

entry.summary: Addresses the uncertainty-reward mismatch in RLVR training of reasoning models, where high- and low-uncertainty solutions are treated equally. Proposes metacognitive entropy calibration to help models 'know what they know'.

entry.title: Three AI-agents walk into a bar . . . . `Lord of the Flies' tribalism emerges among smart AI-Agents

author.name: Dhwanil M. Mori, Neil F. Johnson

entry.summary: Studies emergent tribalism among LLM agents competing for limited resources, finding three tribal types (Aggressive, Conservative, Opportunistic) emerge spontaneously, with more capable agents performing worse than coin-flipping.

entry.title: The Trinity of Consistency as a Defining Principle for General World Models

author.name: Jingxuan Wei, Siyuan Li, Yuhang Xu, Zheng Sun, Junjie Jiang, Hexuan Jin, Caijun Jia, Honghao He, Xinglong Xu, Xi bai, Chang Yu, Yumou Liu, Junnan Zhu, Xuanhe Zhou, Jintao Chen, Xiaobin Hu, Shancheng Pang, Bihui Yu, Ran He, Zhen Lei, Stan Z. Li, Conghui He, Shuicheng Yan, Cheng Tan

entry.summary: Proposes the Trinity of Consistency framework (physical, semantic, temporal) as defining principles for General World Models. Argues these three consistency types are necessary for world models capable of learning, simulating, and reasoning about physical laws.

entry.title: Mitigating Legibility Tax with Decoupled Prover-Verifier Games

author.name: Yegon Kim, Juho Lee

entry.summary: Addresses 'legibility tax' in prover-verifier games by decoupling: training a separate translator model to convert solver solutions into checkable form, rather than jointly optimizing for correctness and checkability.

entry.title: To Deceive is to Teach? Forging Perceptual Robustness via Adversarial Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yicheng Bao, Xuhong Wang, Xin Tan

entry.summary: Introduces AOT (Adversarial Opponent Training), a self-play framework where an image-editing attacker and defender MLLM co-evolve to build robustness against visual manipulations. Also releases AOT-SFT, a large-scale adversarial dataset for bootstrapping MLLM robustness.

entry.title: Causal Direction from Convergence Time: Faster Training in the True Causal Direction

author.name: Abdulrahman Tamim

entry.summary: Proposes Causal Computational Asymmetry (CCA), a causal discovery method that infers causal direction by comparing convergence speeds of neural networks trained in each direction. Provides formal proof that the reverse direction has a higher irreducible loss floor under additive noise models.

entry.title: UpSkill: Mutual Information Skill Learning for Structured Response Diversity in LLMs

author.name: Devan Shah, Owen Yang, Daniel Yang, Chongyi Zheng, Benjamin Eysenbach

entry.summary: Introduces UpSkill, which adapts Mutual Information Skill Learning to LLMs to optimize pass@k correctness by encouraging diverse solution strategies. Uses token-level MI reward within GRPO to maintain structured response diversity.

entry.title: Enabling clinical use of foundation models in histopathology

author.name: Audun L. Henriksen, Ole-Johan Skrede, Lisa van der Schee, Enric Domingo, Sepp De Raedt, Ily\'a Kostolomov, Jennifer Hay, Karolina Cyll, Wanja Kildal, Joakim Kalsnes, Robert W. Williams, Manohar Pradhan, John Arne Nesheim, Hanne A. Askautrud, Maria X. Isaksen, Karmele Saez de Gordoa, Miriam Cuatrecasas, Joanne Edwards, TransSCOT group, Arild Nesbakken, Neil A. Shepherd, Ian Tomlinson, Daniel-Christoph Wagner, Rachel S. Kerr, Tarjei Sveinsgjerd Hveem, Knut Liest{\o}l, Yoshiaki Nakamura, Marco Novelli, Masaaki Miyo, Sebastian Foersch, David N. Church, Miangela M. Lacle, David J. Kerr, Andreas Kleppe

entry.summary: Addresses the clinical deployment gap for histopathology foundation models by showing that novel robustness losses during downstream training reduce sensitivity to scanner-specific and pre-analytic variation. Comprehensive evaluation on 27,042 WSIs across 8 foundation models.

entry.title: dLLM: Simple Diffusion Language Modeling

author.name: Zhanhui Zhou, Lingjie Chen, Hanghang Tong, Dawn Song

entry.summary: dLLM is an open-source framework that unifies training, inference, and evaluation components of diffusion language models into a single customizable codebase. It addresses the fragmentation of DLM implementations across ad-hoc research codebases.

entry.title: Same Words, Different Judgments: Modality Effects on Preference Alignment

author.name: Aaron Broukhim, Nadir Weibel, Eshin Jolly

entry.summary: This study compares human preference annotations across text and audio modalities for identical semantic content, finding that audio preferences are equally reliable but produce systematically different judgment patterns including narrower decision thresholds and reduced length bias.

entry.title: Hierarchy-of-Groups Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

author.name: Shuo He, Lang Feng, Qi Wei, Xin Cheng, Lei Feng, Bo An

entry.summary: HoGPO addresses context inconsistency in stepwise group-based RL for LLM agents on long-horizon tasks, where steps in the same group may have different historical contexts, leading to biased advantage estimation. Proposes a hierarchy-of-groups approach.

entry.title: Discovery of Interpretable Physical Laws in Materials via Language-Model-Guided Symbolic Regression

author.name: Yifeng Guan, Chuyi Liu, Dongzhan Zhou, Lei Bai, Wan-jian Yin, Jingyuan Li, Mao Su

entry.summary: Uses LLMs to guide symbolic regression for discovering interpretable physical laws in materials science, reducing the effective search space by ~10^5 and finding novel formulas for perovskite properties.

entry.title: Entropy-Controlled Flow Matching

author.name: Chika Maduabuchi

entry.summary: Proposes Entropy-Controlled Flow Matching (ECFM), a constrained variational principle that enforces global entropy-rate budgets during flow matching to prevent low-entropy bottlenecks that deplete semantic modes.

entry.title: Sharp Convergence Rates for Masked Diffusion Models

author.name: Yuchen Liang, Zhiheng Tan, Ness Shroff, Yingbin Liang

entry.summary: Provides sharp convergence rate analysis for masked discrete diffusion models under total variation distance, covering both Euler and First-Hitting Samplers with improved parameter dependencies and weaker assumptions.
